# 17 — W52: Expansions on top of spec 16

This spec collects every widening and deepening of existing mechanics ordered after spec 16. Each request of the user lands here as a batch of wave **W52**, written to be integrated completely under the completion contract of spec 13 J.19, the standing rules of `CLAUDE.md` and the thirteen elements of spec 16 Appendix 16.L.

The spec has 112 parts. Batches 1–99 widen the mechanics the user named; the deepening passes (Parts 100–109) read every value of batches 1–93 again for depth; Part 111 is the integration plan; Part 112 is batch 100, the world below, written after the plan and placed in it (52.660); Appendix 17.A lists every value added, 17.B the steps that integrate each, 17.C the closing audit.

## Part 0. Scope, baseline and ground rules

### 0.1 Baseline

Every section of specs 13 and 16 (W1–W51) counts as built. "Current" in this spec describes the world after spec 16. Where a defect lives in code that no spec 16 section touches, it is named as found in the code on 2026-11-16 and closed here.

Rows stand in the order they were written. Where later rows widen the same value again, the later row gives the count after W52; Appendix 17.A gives each enum's final list.

### 0.2 Numbering

- Wave **W52**; sections `52.1…` continue across batches.
- Foundations **F59…** (spec 16 ends at F58), couplings **C80…**, loops **L126…**, acceptance stories **AS69…**, decisions **K.54…**, reference lanes **R54…**.
- **Coverage.** The first step of W52 extends `scripts/spec_coverage.py`, `scripts/check_spec_depth.py` and `scripts/check_inventory.py` to read this file. `spec_coverage.py write` produces `17-coverage.md` with the columns and rules of `16-coverage.md`, and the commit gate checks it.

### 0.4 Ground rules

Spec 13 G1–G11, spec 16 0.4 and 0.5 (function over look), and rules 1–8 of `CLAUDE.md` bind every section. In particular:

- Every number is a rule key in a named namespace with default and range, editable in World Rules, with a band in `13-balance-bands.json`.
- Enum values are function words. No text the model sees carries example lists, sample sentences or default names. Season names, year names and tradition names come from the world's languages and typed fields.
- Every new value is read by the engine (`check_enum_values_read.py`, 47.7), listed in full by every tool text that lists its enum (`test_tool_enum_lists.py`), labelled with icon and tone in the frontend label map (`check_label_maps.py`), and shown through its label (`check_raw_enums.mjs`).
- Every new or widened table fills the layers of spec 16 6.6: changes, moments, places, terms, history, search and control.

### 0.5 Defects found while writing batch 1

No section of spec 16 touches these. Each is closed in the section named, with a regression test that fails on the old code and a mechanical guard.

| # | Defect | Closed by |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `remove_season` renumbers only `tradition_profiles.season_position`. Gatherings, birth signs, forced weather, event profiles and every other column holding a season position keep a position that has moved or no longer exists. | F59 |
| D2 | Weather families are hand-written `frozenset`s in 14 modules (`environment/weather.py`, `phases/environment.py`, `military/{battle,clash,duels,naval,vessels,campaign}.py`, `demography/biology.py`, `intrigue/schemes.py`, `catalog/units.py` and others). A new weather kind misses each of them silently. | F60 |
| D3 | Weather factors per unit family live twice: literal multipliers in `catalog/units.py` `WEATHER_EFFECTS` (against G1) and rule keys in `rules/registry/battle_tables.py`. | F60 |
| D4 | Calendar slot openness is written twice with different meanings: `engine/lore/rites.py` `season_of` (holy day not limited to the caster's world, midwinter by temperature, campaign meaning "at war") and `engine/lore/traditions.py` `slot_fits` (holy day on the world, midwinter by growth, campaign by season fitness). | F61 |
| D5 | Default season names are fixed English words in `engine/environment/seasons.py` (`SEASON_SHAPES`, `ICE_SHAPE`), so every world's seasons carry the same images whatever its seed (rule 2). | 52.1 |
| D6 | Impact winters, eruption cold and supernova cold are one-shot `cold_snap` calls (`cosmos/impacts.py`, `phases/disasters.py`, `cosmos/remnants.py`), apart from the long-season mechanic, with no forecast, no named year and no end. | 52.3 |
| D7 | A long summer has no effect: `bite` and `winter_share` read winter only. | 52.3 |
| D8 | `irregular_seasons` is keyed by `world_id`, so a world holds one long season at a time. | 52.3 |
| D9 | Terrain families are hand-written `frozenset`s of `TerrainKind` in 27 modules (about 80 sets, among them `catalog/{bonds,dangers,effect_packages,tenets,units,methods,eras,mind}.py`, `engine/{demography,ecology,economy,military,storyteller,vehicles,structures,industry,disease}/…` and `tools/mortal/registry.py`). A new terrain kind misses each of them silently. | F62 |
| D10 | Passability special-cases movement modes by hand: `GROUND_MODES` and `ROAD_MODES` sets, `boat` and `flying` computed outside `MODE_SENSITIVITY`, and one terrain base for every ground mode. A terrain has no passage value of its own per mode, and a new mode has nowhere to go. | F63 |
| D11 | Danger and hazard chronicle lines in `catalog/dangers.py` are fixed sentences that carry images ("Strange lights and voices…", "Fever rose from the ground…", "The sucking ground…"), and the label "Strange phenomena" forces strangeness (rule 2). | F64 |
| D12 | Planetary cycles are fixed columns of `world_cycles` (`carbon`, `water`, `nutrients` and their `_in` and `_out`, listed again in `CYCLE_FIELDS`), so a new cycle means new columns in every reader, and the water cycle counts water on worlds whose surface liquid is another. | F66 |

A new ground, gear or rank misses each of them, and the gear-ban law bans no gear in particular. | F67 |
| D14 | Diet, stage, role and biochemistry families are hand-written and disagree: "hunters" is `{carnivore, omnivore, soul}` in `domain/enums/ecology.py`, `{carnivore, omnivore, scavenger}` in `nature/senses.py` and `{carnivore, omnivore}` in `ecology/domestication.py` and `ecology/profiles.py`; "kept" stages are written four times (`KEPT_STAGES`, `BRED`, two `HOUSED`); `pets.HUNTING_USES` stands in for a hunting role with `{guard, war}`; eighteen such sets in all. | F68 |

| D40 | 52.639 re-adds `CultivationMethod` grafting and partnering, which spec 16 `cultivation` and `binding` already hold | 52.639 |
| D41 | Spec 13 6.1 names six strata in prose ("aquifers, cavern layers 1–3, a magma sea, a deep underworld") but gives them no values, so 52.30 and 52.442 widen an enum whose first six values do not exist and "cavern layers 1–3" has no order a map can choose | 52.663: `aquifer`, `cavern_upper`, `cavern_middle`, `cavern_lower`, `magma_sea`, `deep_underworld`, with depth ranks |

## Part 1. Shared foundations

### F59. Season positions are one registry

**State.** `catalog/season_positions.py` holds `SEASON_POSITIONS`: one entry per column that holds the position of a world season (table, column, nullable, how the row finds its world). It covers at least `tradition_profiles.season_position`, `forced_weather.season_position`, `gatherings.season`, `birth_signs.season`, `event_profiles.start_season` and `event_profiles.end_season`. The implementer classifies every other integer column named `season`, `season_index` or `*_season` by reading its writers: a world-season position joins `SEASON_POSITIONS`; an in-epoch step counter (`convoys.season`, `army_movements.season`, `supply_flows.season`, `camps.season_index` if so found) joins `SEASON_STEPS` in the same module.

**Behaviour.** `add_season`, `remove_season` and `reorder_seasons` in `engine/environment/time_control.py` build a mapping from old to new position and call `remap_positions(session, world_id, mapping)`, which rewrites every column of `SEASON_POSITIONS`. A position whose season was removed becomes null where the column is nullable, and otherwise takes the season that now holds its index (clamped to the last season).

**Integrity.** `season_positions_valid` in `services/integrity`: every registered column is below its world's season count.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_season_positions.py` fails when a table column whose name matches the season pattern is in neither list, and when code writes a registered column outside the remap and the record's own writers.

**Test.** `tests/engine/environment/test_season_positions.py`: removing a season moves a gathering and a birth sign with it (fails on the old code).

### F60. Weather draws and weather traits are typed in the catalogue

**State.** `catalog/weather.py` `WeatherSpec` gains:

- `draw: WeatherDraw`. Selects the weight function in `weather_weights`, replacing the `if kind in COLD_KINDS … elif …` chain. Values: `cold`, `hot`, `dry`, `dry_hot`, `wet`, `wet_liquid`, `clear`, `even`, `aurora`, `magic`, `ash`, `void`, `eclipse`, `freezing_clear` (52.2), `freezing_wet` (52.2).
- `traits: frozenset[WeatherTrait]`. Every reader that used a hand-written set reads a trait. `WeatherTrait` values and the sets they replace:

| Trait | Replaces | Members after W52 |
|---|---|---|
| `cold` | `weather.COLD_KINDS`, `biology.WINTER`, folk cold-blooded reading | snow, blizzard, frost, ice_storm |
| `snow_cover` | `clash.WINTER`, `battle.SNOW` | snow, blizzard |
| `icy` | new | frost, ice_storm |
| `wet` | `weather.WET_KINDS`, `duels.WET`, `battle.RAIN` (by intersection with `liquid`) | rain, downpour, storm, fog, hail, snow, blizzard, ice_storm |
| `liquid` | `weather.LIQUID_KINDS` | rain, downpour, ice_storm |
| `hot` | `weather.HOT_KINDS` | heat_wave |
| `dry` | `weather.DRY_KINDS` | drought_wind, sandstorm |
| `windy` | `naval.WINDY`, `vessels.WINDY`, `battle.WIND` | storm, drought_wind, sandstorm |

| `covering` | `schemes.COVERING_WEATHER` | fog, blizzard, sandstorm |

The exact current membership of each set is kept for the existing kinds; the table above lists the sets as found and must be checked against the code when the set is replaced.

- The weather × unit family table moves into the catalogue as `WeatherSpec.unit_factors`, every value a rule key in `battle_tables` (`{weather}_{family}_pct`, one key for each pair the old literal table or the old keys held). `catalog/units.py` `WEATHER_EFFECTS` and `rule_tables.py` read it; the literal multipliers go.
- The W48 authored layer and property catalogue of `WeatherKind` (48.B) read the same spec, so authored weather kinds inherit draw, traits and factors from their category.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_weather_sets.py` fails on any literal collection of two or more `WeatherKind` members, and on any mapping keyed by `WeatherKind`, outside `catalog/weather.py`, migrations and tests. `WEATHER` is a `total()` catalogue (`test_total_tables.py`). `tests/unit/test_weather_traits.py` fails when a kind lacks a draw, traits or unit factors, or when a trait has no reader.

### F61. Calendar slots are one catalogue and one function

**State.** `catalog/calendar_slots.py` holds `SLOTS`, a `total()` catalogue: per `CalendarSlot` its `opening: SlotOpening`, its `effects: frozenset[TraditionEffectKind]` (replacing `traditions.SLOT_EFFECTS`), its `lean: ValueAxis` (the preference lean that `mind/preferences.py` today gives only to `harvest`) and its label.

**Behaviour.** `engine/lore/calendar_slots.py` `slot_open(ctx, world_id, slot, holder_id) -> SlotState(open: bool, reason: str | None)` is the only test of whether a slot comes. `rites.season_of` and `traditions.slot_fits` are removed and both callers use it. The meanings are fixed once:

- `holy_day` opens on a sky event over the holder's world this epoch, or where the holder's people keep a calendar with holy days.
- `campaign` opens where a season of the world is fit for war (`traditions.season_campaign`). Being at war, which `season_of` read as `campaign`, becomes a rite requirement of its own: `war` in `rite_profiles.requirements` (bool), with its own unmet reason.
- `midwinter` opens where the coldest season's temperature shift is at most `-traditions.midwinter_cold` and its growth is at most `traditions.dead_growth`.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_calendar_slots.py` fails when code outside the two modules above compares with or keys on a `CalendarSlot` member. `tests/engine/lore/test_calendar_slots.py` covers every slot and shows that a holy day on another world no longer opens a rite's slot (fails on the old code).

## Part 2. Batch 1 — seasons, weather and the calendar

### 52.1 Up to eight seasons

**Builds on.** Spec 13 F2.2 (`world_seasons`, `season_count`), `engine/environment/seasons.py`, `time_control.py`, `cosmos/orbits.py`, F58.6 moments by the world's calendar, 50.23 snowpack and melt seasons, 50.28 forecasts by season.

**Current.** `season_count` is 1–6 (check `season_count_range`, `SEASONS_MAX = 6`). `season_count_for` steps through four tilt thresholds and returns six above the last. `SEASON_SHAPES` gives one fixed table per count with English names and a wetness mark, `WARMEST` gives the warmest position for counts 1–6, and `orbits.py` doubles the count for chaotic orbits up to `max(SEASON_SHAPES)`. All seasons of a world are equal in length.

**State.**

- `constants/calendar.py` `SEASONS_MAX = 8`. The `worlds` check becomes 1–8. `WorldSeasonsView` serves `seasons_max` so the frontend reads the cap from the server.
- `world_seasons.share_pct` (1–100): the season's share of the year; the shares of a world sum to 100.
- `season_phase(seasons) -> dict[int, SeasonPhase]`, a pure function served on every season view (not stored): `warmth` (`SeasonWarmth`: `coldest`, `cold`, `cooling`, `even`, `warming`, `warm`, `warmest`) and `water` (`SeasonWater`: `dry`, `even`, `wet`), from the shifts against the world's other seasons.
- `NameKind.SEASON` in `language/generator.py`.
- `SEASON_SHAPES` and `ICE_SHAPE` lose their names and become wetness patterns; `WARMEST` gains 7 and 8.

**Behaviour.**

1. `season_count_for` reads six thresholds; above `seven_seasons_below_tilt` a world has eight seasons. `orbits.py` caps its doubling at `SEASONS_MAX`.
2. `season_drafts` works for 1–8: temperature by the cosine of the year as today, wetness by the pattern (the dry season at the warmest, the wet season `seasons.wet_offset` seasons after it), and shares equal except that with six or more seasons each `warming` and `cooling` season takes `seasons.transition_share_pct` and the rest share the remainder.
3. Every draft season is named by the world namer from the world's language (`NameKind.SEASON`). A one-season world's season is named the same way. The deepener may rename from canon.
4. Readers that pick a season for a sampled year (harvest sampling, `weather_year`, campaign seasons, forecasts, gathering dates, birth signs) draw by share through `pick_season(seasons, rng)`.
5. Moments (F58.6) find their season by day of year against the cumulative shares.
6. Adding a season takes its share from the others in proportion; removing gives it back in proportion; editing one share rebalances the unheld others. Every change remaps positions (F59).
7. Readers of coldest, wettest and hottest (`HazardSeason`, `hazards.season_for`, monsoon seasons, midwinter and midsummer slots) read `season_phase` and work for every count.
8. Worlds whose world view has no seasons, and tidally locked worlds, keep one season.

**Rules.** Namespace `seasons`:

| Key | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `seasons.six_seasons_below_tilt` | 65 | 0–90 |
| `seasons.seven_seasons_below_tilt` | 78 | 0–90 |
| `seasons.transition_share_pct` | 8 | 1–50 |
| `seasons.wet_offset` | 1 | 0–7 |

The ascending chain in `rules/constraints.py` grows to `two < three < four < five < six < seven ≤ tilt_max`.

**Incidents.** `season.added`, `season.removed`, `season.reordered`, `season.reshaped` (share or values changed), each with the world, the season and the values before and after (F58.5).

**Agent tools.**

- Son `add_season` (`world_id`, `name`, `temperature_shift`, `rain_shift`, `growth`, `travel`, `campaign`, `share_pct`, `position`), refused at eight with "That world already keeps eight seasons."
- Son `reorder_seasons` (`world_id`, `order`) unchanged.
- Son `reshape_season` (new: `season_id`, `share_pct`, `temperature_shift`, `rain_shift`, `reason`).
- Mortal `forecast_seasons` and mortal `forecast` (50.28) take season positions 0–7.

**God levers.** `seasons:add`, `seasons:edit` (with `share_pct`), `seasons:remove`, `seasons:reorder`, `seasons:release`, all through the remap.

**Screens.** `WorldSeasonsSection` and `SeasonCalendarPanel`: a season wheel of up to eight segments sized by share, with warmth and water medallions; a share slider per season with a running total; add disabled at eight ("A world keeps at most eight seasons") and remove disabled at one ("A world keeps at least one season"); a world without seasons shows the section disabled with its world-view reason.

**Context.** `SeasonLine` gains `share_pct`, `warmth`, `water`, `temperature_shift`, `rain_shift` and `travel`.

**Codex and book.** A "Seasons" table in every world entry (order, name, warmth, water, share of the year, temperature, rain, growth, travel, campaign, held) and a season wheel figure in the book.

**Integrity.** Positions run 0…n−1 without gaps; n equals `season_count` when set; shares sum to 100; F59.

**Legacy.** Fixup `seasons.w52_shares`: equal shares, the remainder to the warmest season. Unedited seasons whose name is one of the old `SEASON_SHAPES` or `ICE_SHAPE` names are renamed by the namer.

**Reach.** Every world, planet or moon, in every era. Stars, the Creator, sons, foreign gods and entities have no seasons of their own; they read the seasons of their world.

**Couplings.** Harvest, weather draws, war seasons, travel, traditions and slots, births and signs, hazards, forecasts, snowpack and melt, moments.

### 52.2 Frost and ice storm

**Builds on.** Spec 13 F2.3 (weather on demand, `weather_effects`), F60, 50.23 frozen ground and snowpack, 50.28 weather works, F51 networks, 48.B authored weather layer.

**Current.** Seventeen weather kinds. Cold weather means snow or blizzard. Nothing models a clear freezing night that kills blossoms and sprouts, or rain that freezes on contact and coats ground, trees, hulls and lines.

**State.**

- `WeatherKind.frost` (draw `freezing_clear`, traits `cold`, `icy`, `extreme`, favoured by domain `ice`).
- `WeatherKind.ice_storm` (draw `freezing_wet`, traits `cold`, `icy`, `wet`, `liquid`, `storm`, `slowing`, `heavy`, `extreme`, favoured by domains `ice` and `storm`).
- Eight effect keys and a weight for each, and unit factors for each in `battle_tables` (F60).
- Enum check constraints rebuilt on every column typed by `WeatherKind` (`notable_years.weather`, `forced_weather.kind`, the battleground weather column in `warfare.py`, the 48.B authored layer's category column, and any other found by `grep enum_type(WeatherKind`).

**Behaviour.**

1. Frost is drawn where the temperature lies within `weather.frost_band` above the cold threshold or below it and the air is dry, with weight × `weather.frost_transition_pct` in `warming` and `cooling` seasons.
2. Ice storm is drawn where the temperature lies within `weather.glaze_band` of the cold threshold and the air is wet.
3. Frost in a `warming` season destroys `weather.late_frost_growth_pct` of that season's growth in the sampled year. Every frost deepens frozen ground (50.23) by `weather.frost_ground_depth`.
4. Ice storm harms structures and roads by `weather.ice_storm_structure_harm`, takes `weather.ice_storm_timber_loss_pct` of forest cover and perennial crops, causes an outage in each wired, relay or broadcast network of the region with `weather.ice_storm_outage_pct` (F51), kills `weather.ice_storm_herd_loss_pct` of herds, and raises vessel danger at sea by `weather.icing_hull_pct`.
5. Every trait reader picks the two kinds up: marches slow, schemes lose pursuit, cold-blooded peoples weaken, vessels face storm danger, hard weather years are named (52.4).
6. Weather works (50.28) with aim `cold` produce frost in dry regions and ice storm in wet regions near freezing. Forecast methods predict both.

| `weather.frost_footing` | −15 | −100–100 |
| `weather.frost_cold` | 50 | 0–100 |
| `weather.frost_heat` | 0 | 0–100 |
| `weather.frost_wet` | 0 | 0–100 |
| `weather.frost_wind` | 0 | 0–100 |
| `weather.frost_morale` | −5 | −100–100 |
| `weather.frost_growth` | −45 | −100–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_weight` | 3 | 0–10000 |
| `weather.ice_storm_visibility` | −35 | −100–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_footing` | −85 | −100–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_cold` | 70 | 0–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_heat` | 0 | 0–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_wet` | 45 | 0–100 |
| `weather.ice_storm_wind` | 25 | 0–100 |

| `weather.ice_storm_growth` | −35 | −100–100 |

### 52.3 Six causes of long winters and summers

**Builds on.** `engine/environment/long_seasons.py`, `irregular_seasons`, `winter_forecasts`, `cosmos/impacts.py`, `phases/disasters.py`, `cosmos/remnants.py`, `cosmos/starlife.py`, 50.22 space weather, 50.28 observation, famine lore.

**Current.** One row per world. `begin` starts a cycling spell from a natural law or a chaotic orbit, or from a god through `unsettle_seasons`. Spells alternate without end while the cause holds. Winters cut harvest and food; summers do nothing (D7). Impacts, large eruptions and supernovae cool worlds once through `cold_snap` (D6).

**State.**

- `SeasonCause` gains `impact`, `eruption`, `stellar` (six values).
- `SeasonSpellShape`: `cycling` (alternates while the cause holds) and `single` (one spell that ends).
- `LongSeasonReach`: `world`, `north`, `south`.
- `irregular_seasons` is rebuilt with an `id` key and several rows per world: `world_id`, `cause`, `shape`, `spell`, `spell_started_epoch`, `spell_length`, `severity`, `reach`, `source_impact_id`, `source_region_id`, `source_star_id`, `by_node_id`, `locked`.
- `winter_forecasts.long_season_id` replaces the world as the forecast's subject; unique per long season and people.

**Behaviour.**

1. **Impact.** A struck impact of size at least `long_seasons.impact_size_min` begins a single winter on its world: length from `winter_epochs`, severity size × `impact_severity_per_size_pct`. Smaller impacts keep the cold snap. `impact_winters` stops calling `cold_snap` for impacts that began a spell.
2. **Eruption.** An eruption of strength at least `eruption_strength_min` begins a single winter: length between `eruption_length_min` and `eruption_length_max`, severity strength × `eruption_severity_pct`. Reach is the world at strength `eruption_world_strength` or above, otherwise the hemisphere of the source region; regions outside the reach feel `far_share_pct` of it. Smaller eruptions keep the cold snap.
3. **Stellar.** A star whose brightness falls by at least `stellar_dim_pct` in an epoch, a lasting negative luminosity modifier, a black sun over a world, or a supernova near enough to cool it begins a single winter on every world lit by that star (moons through `planet_of`, `check_moon_orbits.py`). A rise of at least `stellar_bright_pct` begins a single summer. The spell ends when its length runs out or brightness returns within the threshold.
4. **Orbit, natural law, divine** keep cycling as today. A god's spell may be cycling or single.
5. **Long summer effects.** Regions above the hot threshold or below the dry threshold lose `summer_harvest_pct` × severity of harvest; regions below the cold threshold gain `summer_cold_gain_pct` × severity. While a summer spell lasts, regions in reach shift by `+summer_heat_shift` temperature and `−summer_rain_shift` rain, hot and dry weather weighs `weather_shift_pct` × severity more, and disease season factors rise by `summer_sickness_pct`.
6. **Long winter effects.** As today (harvest share, food loss eased by forecasts, storage and famine foods), plus `−winter_cold_shift` temperature while the spell lasts (lifted when it ends), cold weather (trait `cold`, with frost and ice storm) weighing `weather_shift_pct` × severity more, and season travel and campaign cut by `travel_winter_pct` and `campaign_winter_pct`.
7. **Stacking.** Several spells on one world combine: the strongest severity plus `stacking_share_pct` of each other spell of the same kind; a winter and a summer offset by their difference.
8. **Forecasts** are made per long season. Single spells whose source a people observed (50.28 methods) are forecast with error cut by `forecast_known_source_pct`.
9. **Ending.** `lost_cause` per cause: natural law gone, orbit no longer chaotic, single spell elapsed, star recovered. A god's spell ends by length or by the god.
10. The first year of a single spell is a named year (52.4).

**Rules.** Namespace `long_seasons` (existing keys kept):

| Key | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `long_seasons.impact_size_min` | 30 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.impact_severity_per_size_pct` | 80 | 0–200 |
| `long_seasons.eruption_strength_min` | 70 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.eruption_world_strength` | 90 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.eruption_length_min` | 1 | 1–20 |
| `long_seasons.eruption_length_max` | 3 | 1–40 |
| `long_seasons.eruption_severity_pct` | 60 | 0–200 |
| `long_seasons.far_share_pct` | 25 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.stellar_dim_pct` | 10 | 1–100 |
| `long_seasons.stellar_bright_pct` | 10 | 1–100 |
| `long_seasons.stacking_share_pct` | 30 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.summer_harvest_pct` | 30 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.summer_cold_gain_pct` | 15 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.summer_heat_shift` | 10 | 0–50 |
| `long_seasons.summer_rain_shift` | 10 | 0–50 |
| `long_seasons.summer_sickness_pct` | 10 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.winter_cold_shift` | 15 | 0–50 |
| `long_seasons.weather_shift_pct` | 50 | 0–200 |
| `long_seasons.travel_winter_pct` | 30 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.campaign_winter_pct` | 40 | 0–100 |
| `long_seasons.forecast_known_source_pct` | 50 | 0–100 |

The pairs `eruption_length_min ≤ eruption_length_max` and `eruption_strength_min ≤ eruption_world_strength` join `rules/constraints.py`.

**Incidents.** Kept: `seasons.irregular`, `seasons.winter`, `seasons.summer`, `seasons.settled`, `climate.cold_snap` (below the thresholds). New: `seasons.spell_began` (facts: cause, shape, spell, severity, length, reach; roles: world, source, by), `seasons.spell_ended`, `seasons.summer_drought` (harvest lost under a long summer), `seasons.forecast_made`.

**Agent tools.**

- Son `unsettle_seasons` (`world_id`, `shape`, `spell`, `length`, `severity`, `reason`).
- Son `lengthen_winter` (`long_season_id`, `epochs`, `reason`).
- Son `end_long_season` (new: `long_season_id`, `reason`).
- Son `call_impact` and the eruption disaster act reach impact and eruption spells through their sources.
- Mortal `forecast_seasons` (`long_season_id`).

**God levers.** `irregular_season:create` (world, cause, shape, spell, severity, length, reach, source), `irregular_season:edit`, `irregular_season:delete` and `irregular_season:forecast` by row id; `winter_forecast:*` linked to the row.

**Screens.** A "Long seasons" panel in the world drawer: one card per spell with cause medallion, spell icon, severity bar, epochs left, reach and a link to its source (impact, region or star); a create flow in titled steps (cause → source picker filtered by cause, disabled with its reason where no source exists → shape, fixed for impact, eruption, stellar, orbit and natural law → spell → severity and length); forecasts per people. `features/tales/labels.ts` gains labels, icons and tones for the three causes, both shapes and the three reaches.

**Context.** Block `long_seasons` for son and mortal turns: cause, source name, shape, spell, severity, epochs left, reach, and the forecast the people holds.

**Codex and book.** "Long seasons" in every world entry (cause, source, shape, spell, severity, began, ends, reach, held) with forecasts per people; impact, region and star entries list the spells they caused.

**Integrity.** Single shape for impact, eruption and stellar; cycling for orbit and natural law; the source exists and belongs to the world (impact on the world, region in the world, star lighting the world through `root_of`); a forecast's long season is on the forecast's world.

**Legacy.** The migration rebuilds `irregular_seasons` and `winter_forecasts`; existing rows become `cycling` with reach `world`, and forecasts point to them. Fixup `long_seasons.w52_sources`: struck impacts with `winter_epochs > 0` become single winters with their source.

**Reach.** Every world, planet or moon, in every era. Stars reach it as sources, and regions as eruption sources and as reached regions.

**Couplings.** Harvest, food, famine lore, disease, weather draws, travel and war seasons, forecasts and observation, impacts, eruptions, stellar life, space weather, named years, remembrance.

### 52.4 Named years read the new sources

**Builds on.** `notable_years`, 47.4 (eight kinds), `engine/environment/notable.py`, `phases/environment.py` (`weather_year`, harvest years), `belief_memory.year_legends`, `commemorate_hard_years`, `tradition_profiles.notable_year_id`.

**Current.** Eight kinds after 47.4. Each kind's name pattern is written in more than one module (`notable.py` `EVENT_YEARS`, `control.py` `NOTABLE_NAMES`, literal names in `phases/environment.py`). Only years of hunger found remembrances.

**State.** `catalog/named_years.py`, a `total()` catalogue per `NotableYearKind`: the engine sources that name such a year, its naming parts for F58.10 and its remembrance threshold. Every other copy of a naming pattern goes.

**Behaviour.**

1. Frost and ice storm years are named as weather years through the `extreme` trait when their growth loss reaches `named_years.weather_growth_min`.
2. The first year of a single long season is named: impact and eruption as `disaster`, stellar as `omen`. Cycling spells name years through harvest (hunger, plenty).
3. A people founds a remembrance tradition (slot `remembrance`, 52.5, `notable_year_id` set) for any named year of its regions whose magnitude reaches the kind's threshold. This replaces the hunger-only path of `commemorate_hard_years`.

**Rules.** Namespace `named_years`: `weather_growth_min` 30 [0–100]; `remembered_magnitude_hunger`, `_plenty`, `_weather`, `_pestilence`, `_disaster`, `_discovery`, `_contact`, `_omen`, each 60 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `year.{kind}` (one per kind, F58 facts: source, magnitude, region), `tradition.remembrance_founded`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal tradition founding (`tools/mortal/inputs.py`) and son tradition creation (`creation_inputs.py`) take `notable_year_id` with slot `remembrance`.

**God levers.** `year:force_notable`, `year:edit`, `year:delete` offer eight kinds and the new weather kinds.

**Screens.** `RegionPowers` notable years: eight kinds and nineteen weather kinds with labels; a year's card links to its remembrance traditions.

**Context.** Named years carry kind, source and the remembrances kept for them.

**Codex and book.** Named years in region and world entries with kind, source, magnitude and remembrances.

**Integrity.** A weather year names a weather kind; a remembrance tradition's year lies in the people's regions.

**Legacy.** Fixup `named_years.w52_remembrance`: traditions with `notable_year_id` set and no slot, or slot `holy_day`, take `remembrance`.

**Reach.** Every region and world; peoples remember.

**Couplings.** Weather, long seasons, disasters, sky events, memory and legends, traditions, calendars.

### 52.5 Ten calendar slots

**Builds on.** F61, `tradition_profiles.calendar_slot`, `TraditionEffectKind`, `mind/preferences.py`, rite requirements, calendars, gatherings, markets (50.3), death work (50.12), ecology and species, nomad camps.

**Current.** Five slots: `sowing`, `harvest`, `midwinter`, `campaign`, `holy_day`. Three of them assume a farming people or a cold season, so a world without farms or winters can keep only `campaign` and `holy_day` (rule 2).

**State.**

- `CalendarSlot` gains `new_year`, `midsummer`, `remembrance`, `market`, `wild_harvest` (ten values).
- `TraditionEffectKind` gains `trade` (a fair raises the settlement's trade income and goods flow for the epoch) and `forage` (food from hunting, fishing and gathering, scaled by the region's wild species and pressing on them).
- The rite requirement `war` in `rite_profiles.requirements` (F61).

**Behaviour.** `SLOTS` gives each slot its opening and effects:

| Slot | Opens when | Effects | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sowing` | a `warming` season has growth ≥ `season_growth` | fertility, harvest | `nature` |
| `harvest` | the season after the greenest has growth ≥ `season_growth` | harvest, satisfaction, cohesion | `nature` |
| `midwinter` | F61 | cohesion, placation, food_saved | `kinship` |
| `midsummer` | the warmest season's temperature shift ≥ `midsummer_warm` | cohesion, fertility, satisfaction | `leisure` |
| `campaign` | F61 | martial, cohesion | `martial` |
| `holy_day` | F61 | every effect | `piety` |
| `new_year` | every world with a year | cohesion, satisfaction, rest | `tradition` |
| `remembrance` | the tradition names a named year (52.4) or a remembered death (50.12) of its people | piety, placation, cohesion | `tradition` |
| `market` | the settlement or its region holds a market or a fair gathering, and a season's travel ≥ `market_travel` | trade, satisfaction, cohesion | `wealth` |
| `wild_harvest` | the region's wild game, fish or gathered plants stand at or above `wild_stock_min` | forage, cohesion, satisfaction | `nature` |

Each tradition's `in_season` is set from `slot_open`. A tradition whose slot never opens on its world shows why and lapses as today. Nomad camps move toward the region whose `wild_harvest` slot is open in its season. Every slot leans preferences by its axis.

**Rules.** Namespace `traditions`:

| Key | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `traditions.midwinter_cold` | 5 | 0–50 |
| `traditions.midsummer_warm` | 5 | 0–50 |
| `traditions.market_travel` | 50 | 0–100 |
| `traditions.wild_stock_min` | 20 | 0–100 |
| `traditions.fair_trade_pct` | 10 | 0–100 |
| `traditions.forage_food_pct` | 10 | 0–100 |
| `traditions.forage_pressure` | 3 | 0–50 |

**Incidents.** `tradition.kept` carries the slot as a fact; new `tradition.slot_closed` (a tradition's slot does not come, with the reason) and `tradition.fair_held`, `tradition.forage_taken`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal tradition founding (`calendar_slot`) and son tradition creation list ten slots; rite design takes the requirement `war`.

**God levers.** Tradition and rite editors offer ten slots and the requirement `war` (`test_editable_fields.py`); `tradition:effect` offers `trade` and `forage`.

**Screens.** `TraditionPanel` and the forge: ten slot medallions with icons and tones; a slot that does not come on this world is shown disabled with its reason from `slot_open`, served by the API as `slot_open` and `slot_reason`. People drawers gain a "Year of festivals" strip: the traditions of a people placed on the world's season wheel by slot.

**Context.** Tradition lines carry the slot label and whether it comes this epoch.

**Codex and book.** Tradition entries show slot and opening; people entries show the "Year of festivals" as a designed table in the Codex and a figure in the book.

**Integrity.** A `remembrance` tradition names a named year or a death of its people; a `market` tradition's settlement has a market or fair; F59 for `season_position`.

**Legacy.** Migration rebuilds the `calendar_slot` check (ten values) and the requirement `war` lives in the existing `rite_profiles.requirements`. Fixup `rites.w52_war_need` (`services/integrity/rite_needs.py`): rites whose slot opens in the season fit for war gain the requirement `war`, so they keep their old meaning; 52.4's remembrance fixup.

**Reach.** Every people, settlement and tradition in every era and every kind of world. Slots belong to traditions and rites, so nodes other than peoples, settlements, traditions and rites reach them only through the traditions they keep.

**Couplings.** Traditions, rites, preferences, calendars, gatherings, markets, ecology, nomad camps, named years, death work.

### 52.9 Cross-cutting layers

Each table of batch 1 fills the layers of spec 16 6.6: changes recorded with terms (F58.5, F58.7), happenings with moments and places (F58.6), records readable at any earlier moment (F58.11), nothing folded away (F58.12), every record searchable by its typed fields, and every record created, edited, held, deleted and reverted from the frontend.

### 52.10 Couplings, loops, stories and decisions

**Couplings.**

- C80 Season shares → harvest sampling, weather draws and war windows.
- C81 Frost and ice storm → harvest, networks, structures, forests, herds and vessels.
- C82 Impacts, eruptions and stars → long seasons.
- C83 Long summers → harvest, heat, rain and disease.
- C84 Long seasons and hard weather → named years → remembrance traditions.
- C85 Slots → traditions, trade, foraging and nomad routes.

**Loops.**

- L126 (B) Long winter → hunger → forecasts heeded and stores kept → smaller losses in the next spell.
- L127 (B) Ice storm outages → network repair → fewer outages from the next storm.
- L128 (B) Foraging pressure → wild stocks fall → `wild_harvest` stops opening → stocks recover.

**Acceptance stories.**

- AS69 **The Eighth Season.** A world of high tilt has eight seasons with short transitional ones; a frost in the thaw kills the blossoms; the year is named and a remembrance is founded.
- AS70 **The Glaze.** An ice storm breaks a relay network and the orchards of a valley; an army's march halts; ships at sea ice over.
- AS71 **The Ash Years.** A great eruption brings a hemisphere winter of three epochs; a people that watched the eruption forecasts its end and survives on its stores.
- AS72 **The Dimming.** A star loses brightness; its planet and that planet's moons fall into a stellar winter that ends when the star recovers; the year is named as an omen.
- AS73 **No Fields.** A people with no farms on a world with no winter keeps `market`, `wild_harvest`, `new_year` and `remembrance`; its camps follow the wild harvest.

**Decisions.**

| Id | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| K.54 | Why eight seasons at most? | Tilt yields up to eight; finer divisions of the year are months of a calendar, not seasons. |
| K.55 | Are seasons equal in length? | No. Each holds a share of the year; shares sum to 100. |
| K.56 | How do frost, ice storm, snow and hail differ? | Frost forms on clear freezing nights without falling water; ice storm is rain that freezes on contact in a narrow band around freezing; snow and hail fall frozen. |
| K.57 | One long season per world? | No. Several spells combine: the strongest plus a share of the others; winter and summer offset. |
| K.58 | Does batch 1 add kinds of named year? | No. 47.4 brought them to eight; batch 1 feeds them from the new sources, and the deepening pass adds `peace` and `founding` (52.429). |
| K.59 | What does the `campaign` slot mean? | The season fit for war. Being at war is the rite requirement `war`. |

### 52.11 Execution order (batch 1)

1. Coverage tooling reads this file; `17-coverage.md` is written; inventory rows.
2. Guards (F59–F61), listing every current violation.
3. F60, then 52.2.
4. F59, then 52.1.
5. F61, then 52.5.
6. 52.3 with its migration.
7. 52.4.
8. API, typegen, screens, Codex and book, fixups, then the audit.

The batch is gated once.

## Part 4. Batch 2 foundations

### F62. Terrain traits are typed in the catalogue

**State.** `catalog/terrain.py` holds `TERRAIN`, a `total()` catalogue per `TerrainKind`: label, `traits: frozenset[TerrainTrait]`, `passage: dict[MovementMode, rule key]` (F63), the biomes and world types it is derived from, and the soils it allows. `TerrainTrait` values name what the hand-written sets of D9 mean: `wooded`, `open`, `rough`, `high`, `wet`, `arid`, `cold`, `hot`, `coastal`, `watery`, `underground`, `built`, `ruined`, `confined`, `slippery`, `fertile`, `ambush_cover`, `airless`, `gaseous`, `non_mineral_ground` (the terrains whose ground is not rock, soil, water or ice). Each existing set is replaced by one trait test, with its exact current membership kept for the existing kinds and the new kinds placed by their nature (52.12).

The W48 authored layer and property catalogue of `TerrainKind` (48.B) read the same spec, so authored terrain kinds inherit traits and passage from their category.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_terrain_sets.py` fails on any literal collection of two or more `TerrainKind` members, and on any mapping keyed by `TerrainKind`, outside `catalog/terrain.py`, migrations and tests. `tests/unit/test_terrain_traits.py` fails when a kind lacks traits or a passage value for some mode, or when a trait has no reader.

### F63. Movement modes are typed by medium

**State.** `catalog/movement.py` holds `MOVEMENT`, a `total()` catalogue per `MovementMode`: `medium` (`MovementMedium`: `ground`, `water_surface`, `under_water`, `air`, `through_matter`), `takes_roads`, `takes_bridges`, the feature sensitivities (roughness, forest, wetland, river, cold), and which works help it (roads, bridges, harbours, tunnels, ley lines).

**Behaviour.** `passability_of` reads one loop over `MOVEMENT`: the passage value of the terrain for the mode (`passability.{terrain}_{mode}_pct`, 30 × 8 = 240 rule keys), the mode's feature losses, and the works the mode takes. `GROUND_MODES`, `ROAD_MODES` and the separate `boat` and `flying` paths go. `region_environment.passability` holds a value for all eight modes.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_movement_modes.py` fails on any literal collection or comparison of `MovementMode` members outside `catalog/movement.py` and `engine/environment/profile.py`. `MOVEMENT` and the passage table are `total()` (`test_total_tables.py`).

### F64. Danger and hazard happenings are told from typed fields

**State.** `DangerSpec` and `HazardSpec` lose their fixed sentences and their `words`. Each keeps its typed fields: source or hazard, the injury kind, the maim kind, the weather effect and the season it reads. The label of `phenomena` becomes "Phenomena".

**Behaviour.** Losses to dangers and hazards are F58 incidents (`danger.harm`, `hazard.struck`) with typed facts (source or hazard, target, region, season, count, injury) and are told by F58.10 from those facts, in plain words, in every lore language.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_prompt_bias.py` scans every chronicle template held in `catalog/` modules; `scripts/check_canned_lines.py` treats a per-kind sentence table in a catalogue as a pool. Each gets a case in `backend/tests/unit/test_prompt_bias_rules.py`.

## Part 5. Batch 2 — land, movement and places

### 52.12 Thirty terrain kinds

**Builds on.** Spec 13 F2.1 (`dominant_terrain`, derived from the biome mix and features), F62, F63, `engine/environment/geomorph.py`, `place_terrain.py`, the terrain matrix of war (spec 13, `terrain_effects[TerrainKind][UnitFamily]`), species habitats, 50.23 coasts and frozen ground, 48.B authored terrain layer.

**Current.** 23 kinds. Boreal forest, tropical grassland, salt-tolerant coastal forest, salt flats and dissolved limestone ground fall into neighbouring kinds. Airless bodies and the cloud layers of giant worlds have no terrain of their own, though moons, dwarf planets and giants carry regions (W12).

**State.** `TerrainKind` gains:

| Value | What it is | Traits | Derived where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `taiga` | cold conifer forest | `wooded`, `cold`, `ambush_cover` | forest biome with temperature below the cold threshold |
| `savanna` | warm grassland with scattered trees | `open`, `hot` | grassland biome above the hot threshold with a dry season |
| `mangrove` | salt-tolerant forest on a warm shore | `wooded`, `wet`, `coastal`, `hot`, `ambush_cover` | warm coast with marsh or delta (50.23) |
| `evaporite_flat` | dry lake floor of evaporite | `open`, `arid` | basin below the dry threshold with saline soil |
| `karst` | rock dissolved into sinkholes, caves and hidden rivers | `rough`, `underground` | calcareous soil with high rainfall |
| `regolith_plain` | dust and broken rock without air | `open`, `airless`, `rough` | regions of airless worlds and moons |
| `cloud_deck` | the cloud layer that serves as ground on a giant world | `gaseous`, `open` | regions of gas and ice giants |

The enum checks of every column typed by `TerrainKind` are rebuilt.

**Behaviour.**

1. `geomorph` derives the new kinds by the rules in the table; existing regions are re-derived once (Legacy).
2. Every trait reader picks the new kinds up (F62): ambush and scouting, battle terrain, fuels and extraction, species habitats, people biology, caravans and route dangers, structures, diseases and pests.
3. Passage per mode for each new kind (F63).
4. The terrain × unit family matrix of war gains rows for the seven kinds, each value a rule key.
5. `karst` raises the chance of cave and sinkhole places and of underground routes; `evaporite_flat` yields salt by extraction; `mangrove` shelters harbours from sea waves (51.25) and storms; `regolith_plain` and `cloud_deck` admit only peoples whose biology or works allow life there.

**Rules.** Namespace `terrain`: `terrain.karst_cave_pct` 30 [0–100], `terrain.evaporite_flat_yield` 10 [0–100], `terrain.mangrove_wave_cut_pct` 40 [0–100], `terrain.taiga_cold_below` 0 [−50–50] (offset to the cold threshold), `terrain.savanna_dry_months` 3 [0–12]. Passage keys under F63; unit factors under `battle_tables` (`{terrain}_{family}_pct`).

**Incidents.** `terrain.changed` (a region's terrain re-derived or set, with before and after).

**Agent tools.** Son `shape_land` and region tools list thirty kinds; tool texts that list terrain list every value.

**God levers.** Region environment editor (`region_env:edit` or its existing id) offers thirty kinds.

**Screens.** `features/entity/environment/labels.ts` gains labels, icons and tones for the seven kinds; the atlas terrain layer colours them through theme tokens (`tokenHex`).

**Context.** Region lines carry the terrain label and its traits.

**Codex and book.** Region entries show terrain and traits; the atlas figure renders the new kinds.

**Integrity.** `regolith_plain` only on airless worlds and `cloud_deck` only on giant worlds unless held; terrain in the enum.

**Legacy.** Fixup `terrain.w52_rederive`: unheld regions are re-derived; held regions keep their terrain.

**Reach.** Every region of every world, planet or moon, in every era. Nodes other than regions read their region's terrain.

**Couplings.** Movement, war, habitats, peoples, extraction, places, hazards, dangers, structures.

### 52.13 Seventeen soil kinds

**Builds on.** `region_environment.soil` and `soil_fertility`, 48.8 (fourteen kinds with property names), `engine/environment/shaping.py`, `agrarian/soil.py`, siege works (`siege_depth.py`), sediment (50.23).

**Current.** Fourteen kinds after 48.8. The fertile dark soil of grasslands, the acid soil leached under conifer forest and fine wind-laid soil fall into `loam` and `sand`.

**State.** `SoilKind` gains `humic` (deep dark grassland soil, rich in organic matter), `leached` (acid soil with its nutrients washed down), `silt` (fine soil laid by wind or water). `catalog/soils.py`, a `total()` catalogue: base fertility, drainage, acidity, workability (for digging and siege works), erosion risk and the crops it favours, each a rule key.

**Behaviour.**

1. Soil is derived from terrain, climate and parent rock: `humic` under grassland and savanna with moderate rain, `leached` under taiga and wet conifer forest, `silt` in river valleys, deltas and downwind of deserts. Sediment flows (50.23) lay `silt`.
2. Fertility, crop fit, digging speed, erosion and the soil nutrients of `agrarian/soil.py` read the catalogue for every kind.
3. `humic` soil loses fertility fastest when ploughed without rest (`soils.humic_exhaustion_pct`); `leached` soil gains most from liming and manure; `silt` erodes in wind and flood (feeds scars `eroded`, 52.15).

**Rules.** Namespace `soils`: per kind `{kind}_fertility`, `{kind}_drainage`, `{kind}_workability` (0–100); `soils.humic_exhaustion_pct` 5 [0–50], `soils.leached_amend_gain` 10 [0–50], `soils.silt_erosion_pct` 8 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `soil.changed`, `soil.eroded`.

**Agent tools.** Son land-shaping tools and mortal `improve_soil` (or the existing amendment tool) list seventeen kinds.

**God levers.** Region environment editor offers seventeen kinds.

**Screens.** Soil labels with icons and tones; the region drawer shows the soil's catalogue values.

**Context.** Region lines carry soil and its fertility.

**Codex and book.** Region entries show soil with its values.

**Integrity.** Soil in the enum; `regolith` and `artificial` only where their conditions hold unless held.

**Legacy.** Fixup `soils.w52_rederive` for unheld regions.

**Reach.** Every region with ground; `cloud_deck` regions hold no soil and say so.

**Couplings.** Harvest, crops, digging and siege, erosion, sediment, scars.

### 52.14 Eight movement modes

**Builds on.** F63, `region_environment.passability`, `military/logistics.py`, `military/campaign.py`, `phases/migration.py`, `phases/trade.py`, species and people biology, W44 networks and made minds, spirits.

**Current.** Six modes. Travel beneath the water and travel through solid matter cannot be expressed, so a people that lives under the sea or a being without a body has no way through the map.

**State.** `MovementMode` gains `submerged` (medium `under_water`: moving beneath the surface of seas, lakes and rivers) and `incorporeal` (medium `through_matter`: moving through walls, rock and ground). Which beings may use each mode comes from biology (`species` and people body plans), from powers (W45), from made bodies (W44) and from vessels and vehicles that carry the mode.

**Behaviour.**

1. `submerged` passage is high in `sea`, `coast`, `river_valley`, `mangrove` and `marsh`, falls with ice cover (50.23), and is nil on dry ground. Currents (52.17) and harbours read it.
2. `incorporeal` passage ignores roughness, forest, wetland and rivers; wards, sacred ground, iron and the world's laws (where the world defines them) lower it through rule keys.
3. Armies, migrations, trade routes and caravans choose among the modes their members can use; mixed forces move at the pace of their slowest mode unless split.
4. Supply and logistics read the mode: a submerged army draws supply by water; an incorporeal host needs none of the carried kinds its biology does not use.

**Rules.** Namespace `passability`: the 240 passage keys of F63; `passability.submerged_ice_cut_pct` 60 [0–100], `passability.submerged_current_pct` 30 [0–100], `passability.incorporeal_ward_cut_pct` 70 [0–100], `passability.incorporeal_sacred_cut_pct` 40 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `travel.mode_used` facts on journeys, marches and migrations name the mode.

**Agent tools.** Mortal march, migration and travel tools take `mode` with eight values; son tools that open or close routes list them.

**God levers.** Passability editor offers eight modes; species and people biology editors offer the modes a body can use.

**Screens.** Region drawer passability grid of eight modes with icons; route views show the mode.

**Context.** Region and route lines carry passability per mode.

**Codex and book.** Region entries show the eight-mode passability table.

**Integrity.** Passability holds all eight modes; a being uses only modes its biology, powers or vehicle allow.

**Legacy.** Fixup `passability.w52_modes` recomputes passability for every region.

**Reach.** Every region; every mortal, beast, spirit, made mind, people, army, caravan and vessel by its biology or carrier.

**Couplings.** War, migration, trade, supply, species, powers, wards, ice.

### 52.15 Sixteen scars

**Builds on.** `region_environment.scar`, 48.8 renames, `industry/pollution.py`, `phases/disasters.py`, `sites/digs.py`, `extraction.py`, 47.2.6 hazards, 51.16 war remnants, 50.23 sediment, `succession.py`.

**Current.** Twelve kinds. Land drowned by flood, land poisoned by leaks, weapons or industry, ground emptied by mining and ground worn away by water and wind leave no scar.

**State.** `ScarKind` gains `flooded`, `poisoned`, `mined_out`, `eroded`. `catalog/scars.py`, a `total()` catalogue per kind: fertility loss, passage loss, disease pressure, settlement penalty, decay per epoch and which succession stage it resets to, each a rule key.

**Behaviour.**

1. Floods, spring floods and sea waves leave `flooded`; toxic releases (47.2.6), mass weapons (51.16), pollution above a threshold and designed disease leave `poisoned`; exhausted extraction leaves `mined_out`; `silt` and `sand` soils under clearing, grazing or long summers (52.3) leave `eroded`.
2. Each scar reads its catalogue row while it lasts and fades by its decay; `poisoned` fades only with cleansing works, rites or powers; `mined_out` never fades but can be reworked by later techniques.
3. Succession reads the reset stage (52.22).

**Rules.** Namespace `scars`: per kind `{kind}_fertility_loss`, `{kind}_passage_loss`, `{kind}_decay` (0–100); `scars.pollution_poison_threshold` 70 [0–100], `scars.erosion_clearing_pct` 10 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `scar.made`, `scar.healed`, `scar.cleansed`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `cleanse_land` (`region_id`, `method`); son `wound_land` and `heal_land` list sixteen kinds.

**God levers.** Scar editor (add, edit depth, hold, remove) offers sixteen kinds.

**Screens.** Region drawer scar list with medallions; atlas scar layer.

**Context.** Region lines carry scars with depth.

**Codex and book.** Region entries list scars with depth, cause and age.

**Integrity.** Scar kinds in the enum; depth in range.

**Legacy.** Fixup `scars.w52_causes`: regions with pollution above the threshold gain `poisoned`; exhausted extraction sites give `mined_out`.

**Reach.** Every region and place.

**Couplings.** Disasters, pollution, extraction, war remnants, soil, succession, disease, settlement.

### 52.16 Thirteen memories of the land

**Builds on.** `region_memories`, `engine/environment/memory.py`, `region_control.py`, 52.4 named years, 50.12 death work, F58 incidents.

**Current.** Nine kinds, all harm or holiness. A founding, a peace made, a people driven out or a discovery leaves no memory in the place where it happened.

**State.** `RegionMemoryKind` gains `founding`, `treaty`, `expulsion`, `discovery`. The memory catalogue gives each kind its effects: pilgrimage draw, unrest, claim strength, morale of armies fighting there, settlement desire and the traditions it can seed.

**Behaviour.**

1. Founding a settlement or polity, signing a treaty, expelling a people and a discovery (technique, place, contact) write a memory in the region where it happened, with magnitude from the happening.
2. `founding` strengthens claims of the founders' heirs; `treaty` lowers war will between the signers' heirs in that region and raises grievance when broken there; `expulsion` gives the expelled people a claim and a grievance and may seed a remembrance (52.4, 52.5); `discovery` draws scholars and pilgrims.
3. Memories fade by kind unless kept by traditions.

**Rules.** Namespace `land_memory`: per kind `{kind}_fade` (0–50); `land_memory.founding_claim` 20 [0–100], `land_memory.treaty_war_cut_pct` 20 [0–100], `land_memory.expulsion_grievance` 30 [0–100], `land_memory.discovery_draw` 10 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `memory.written`, `memory.faded`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `commemorate` lists thirteen kinds; son `mark_land` lists them.

**God levers.** Memory editor offers thirteen kinds.

**Screens.** Region drawer "Memories" with medallions per kind.

**Context.** Region lines carry memories.

**Codex and book.** Region entries list memories with cause and age.

**Integrity.** A memory names its incident when it has one.

**Legacy.** Fixup `land_memory.w52_backfill` from past foundings, treaties, expulsions and discoveries in the record.

**Reach.** Every region.

**Couplings.** Claims, war, diplomacy, migration, pilgrimage, traditions, named years.

### 52.17 Twelve danger sources

**Builds on.** `region_dangers`, `engine/environment/dangers.py`, `perils.py`, `route_dangers.py`, F64.

**Behaviour.**

1. `landslide` from roughness, rain and `eroded` or quake history; `exposure` from temperatures beyond the cold or hot threshold and the lack of shelter on routes; `currents` from rivers, coasts, reefs and tides on water routes; `toxic_ground` from volcanic terrain, `poisoned` scars and marsh gases.
2. Dangers harm their targets each epoch through `perils.py`; protections (roads and shelters for exposure, pilots and charts for currents, terraces for landslides, masks or wards for toxic ground) lower them.

**Rules.** Namespace `dangers`: per source `{source}_base` (0–100) and `{source}_protection_cut_pct` (0–100).

Each has terrain traits (F62), a season phase (52.1 `season_phase`), a weather effect, an injury kind and the works that lower it.

**Behaviour.** `mudslide` strikes `rough` and `wet` terrain with `eroded` or cleared slopes; `flash_flood` strikes `arid` terrain and canyons; `thin_ice` strikes frozen rivers, lakes and sea ice in `warming` seasons and harms crossings, caravans and armies on ice.

**Rules.** Namespace `hazards`: per hazard `{hazard}_chance_pct` and `{hazard}_harm` (0–100).

**Builds on.** `SecretKind` (nine after 47.4), `place_secrets`, `engine/environment/secrets.py`, `tools/son/places.py`, 51.21 grave goods, F53 hidden truths.

**Current.** Nine kinds. Hidden ways, sleeping creatures and hidden graves cannot be kept in a place.

**Behaviour.** `hidden_route` adds a passage for those who know it (smugglers, armies, refugees) and is revealed by search or betrayal; `sleeping_beast` wakes by disturbance, digging or a sign and becomes a beast of the wilds (`ecology/beasts`); `hidden_grave` holds grave goods and draws robbers and diggers when found.

**Rules.** Namespace `secrets`: `hidden_route_find_pct` 10 [0–100], `sleeping_beast_wake_pct` 5 [0–100], `hidden_grave_find_pct` 10 [0–100].

### 52.22 Ten succession stages

**Builds on.** `SuccessionStage`, `region_succession`, `engine/environment/succession.py`, `catalog/evolution.py`, 52.15 scars.

**Current.** Seven stages from bare ground through grassland, shrubland, young forest and old forest, with marsh and swamp forest. The pioneer life of bare rock and the filling of open water are absent.

**State.** `SuccessionStage` gains `pioneer` (first life on bare ground), `open_water` (a pond or lake before it fills) and `bog` (wet ground of peat between marsh and swamp forest). `catalog/evolution.py` gives every stage its next stage by climate and its time to advance, each a rule key.

**Behaviour.** Dry path: `bare → pioneer → grassland → shrubland → young_forest → old_forest`. Wet path: `open_water → marsh → bog → swamp_forest`. Climate sets the last stage each region can reach (arid regions stop at grassland or shrubland, cold ones at shrubland or taiga forest). Scars reset to their stage (52.15). `bog` lays `peat` soil.

**Rules.** Namespace `succession`: per stage `{stage}_advance_epochs` (1–100).

**Incidents.** `succession.advanced`, `succession.reset`.

**Agent tools.** Son land tools list ten stages.

**God levers.** Succession editor offers ten stages.

**Screens.** Region drawer stage strip showing the path and current stage.

**Context.** Region lines carry the stage.

**Codex and book.** Region entries show the stage.

**Integrity.** A stage lies on a path its climate allows unless held.

**Legacy.** Fixup `succession.w52_paths`: regions at `bare` with life begin at `pioneer`; lakes begin at `open_water`.

**Reach.** Every region with life.

**Couplings.** Scars, soils, terrain, forests, species, fuels.

### 52.27 Couplings, loops, stories and decisions

**Couplings.** C86 Terrain traits → war, habitats, peoples and works. C87 Movement media → war, migration and trade. C88 Scars → succession and soil. C89 Memories of the land → claims, war and traditions. C90 Danger targets → harvest, ships and structures.

**Loops.** L129 (B) Clearing → erosion → lower harvest → land rested → recovery. L130 (R) Expulsion memory → grievance → war over the region → new memories.

**Acceptance stories.**

- AS74 **The Drowned Road.** A sea people moves an army `submerged` up a delta; a land army on the plateau cannot reach it; a hidden route through a sinkhole decides the war.
- AS75 **The Black Earth.** A people ploughs `humic` soil without rest; it erodes; the scar heals through `pioneer` and grassland over generations.
- AS76 **The Thaw Crossing.** A caravan crosses a frozen river in a `warming` season; the ice gives way; the place keeps the memory and a remembrance is founded.

**Decisions.**

| Id | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| K.60 | Is `ambush` a target? | It stays among the nine as the added harm to the unwarned. |
| K.61 | Where do passage values live? | One rule key per terrain and mode (240), read by one loop over the movement catalogue. |
| K.62 | Who may move `incorporeal`? | Only beings whose biology, powers or made body allow it; the world's laws may lower or forbid it. |

## Part 7. Batch 3 foundation

### F65. Rocks, strata and sediments are typed catalogues

**State.**

- `catalog/rocks.py` holds `ROCKS`, a `total()` catalogue per `RockKind`: hardness (tool tier needed to dig it), porosity (holds water), solubility (forms karst and caves), workability (carving, quarrying), building grade (plain, fine, splendid), the vein materials it may hold and at what depth band, the world types and tectonic settings it forms in, and the soil it weathers into (52.13).
- `catalog/strata.py` holds `STRATA` per `UndergroundStratum`: depth order, what it requires of the world (world type, volcanism, an underworld region, a shell of ice, a hollow body), its biome, the species and peoples it can hold, its access (wells, mines, caves, gates) and its breach effects.
- `catalog/sediments.py` holds `SEDIMENTS` per `SedimentKind`: the carriers that move it, the soil it lays, the fertility it gives, the harbour and canal fill it causes and the rock it becomes over deep time.

Every reader of rock, stratum or sediment reads these catalogues; no reader keeps its own list of kinds.

**Guard.** `scripts/check_deep_sets.py` fails on any literal collection or mapping of two or more members of `RockKind`, `UndergroundStratum`, `SedimentKind`, `CoastForm` or `SealKind` outside their catalogues, migrations and tests. The catalogues are `total()` (`test_total_tables.py`).
