## Part 22. Batch 11 — effect packages

### 52.90 Seventeen effect package categories

**Builds on.** `PackageKind` (F30 effect packages, 48.B authored layer), `catalog/effect_packages.py` (`PackageSpec`: transmissions, onset, stages, cures as a set, visibility, contagion, cure level, heredity), `CurseKind` (47.4), `engine/body/afflictions.py`, `engine/transform/beings.py`, 52.73 ways of passing, sacred-site vengeance, 52.66 temperaments.

**Current.** Fourteen categories: venom, drink dependence, drug dependence, the lunar beast curse, the blood thirst, divine blessing, void taint, possession, trauma, the hunger curse, warping, vis dependence, the doom of a broken geas and the trapped soul. A curse or blessing of luck, a change of shape not tied to the moon, and a charm that compels love or obedience cannot be expressed. Each package already holds a set of cures (`cures: frozenset[CureKind]`), so a package can have several cures; this stays.

**State.** `PackageKind` gains:

| Value | What it installs | Stages | Passing | Cures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fortune` | a lasting shift of luck, with a sign: `+` (blessing) or `−` (curse) | onset, holding, fading | `gaze`, `curse`, `rite`, `birth` (line fortune) | `rite`, `divine`, `quest`, `time` |
| `transformation` | a change of the body into another plan, species or substance (stone, an animal, a plant, a made thing), lasting or recurring by a typed trigger (a season, a sky event, an emotion, a word) | onset, changed, recurring or fixed | `curse`, `bite`, `rite`, `ingestion`, `experience` | `rite`, `quest`, `divine`, `power` |
| `charm` | a compelled bond toward a person or a god: love, obedience or devotion | onset, bound, fading | `ingestion` (potion), `gaze`, `rite`, `intimate` | `rite`, `time`, `medicine`, `power` |

`effect_packages` rows of these categories carry: `fortune_sign`, `fortune_strength`; `transform_target` (body plan, species or substance), `transform_trigger` (`season`, `sky_event`, `emotion`, `word`, `none`), `transform_mind_kept` (whether the changed being keeps its own mind); `charm_target_node_id`, `charm_kind` (`love`, `obedience`, `devotion`).

**Behaviour.**

1. `fortune` shifts the holder's rolls in every chance the engine rolls for them (harvest, battle, trade, birth, travel) by `packages.fortune_roll_pct` × strength, in its sign; a line fortune passes to children.
2. `transformation` turns the body by the target, with the plan's parts, functions and capacities; by its trigger it recurs; if the mind is not kept the being acts by the new form's temperament; the transformed may spread it by bite or blood where the package's passing allows.
3. `charm` sets a bond of its kind toward the target and pushes the charmed being's acts toward the target's wishes; it wears off by time unless renewed; discovery of a charm breaks trust and is a crime where law says so.
4. Sacred-site vengeance (a god cursing those who rob or defile its place) chooses among all seventeen categories by the god's domains, with no category fixed to a domain by our text.
5. Every curse kind (`CurseKind`) installs one package category, so curses and packages agree.

**Rules.** Namespace `packages`: `fortune_roll_pct` 15 [0–100], `fortune_line_pct` 50 [0–100], `transform_recur_pct` 100 [0–100], `charm_strength` 60 [0–100], `charm_fade` 5 [0–50], `charm_renew_cost` 10 [0–500].

**Incidents.** `affliction.fortune_turned`, `affliction.transformed`, `affliction.charmed`, `affliction.charm_broken`, `affliction.charm_renewed` (the charmer pays `charm_renew_cost` each epoch of fading to restore the charm to `charm_strength`).

**Agent tools.** Mortal `bind_with_charm` (`target_id`, `kind`) and `lift_affliction` (`affliction_id`, `cure`); son `curse_with` (`node_id`, `package`, `reason`) and `bless_with` list seventeen.

**God levers.** Package and affliction editors offer seventeen categories with their fields.

**Screens.** Affliction section in `ThingSections`: package medallions with stage, sign, trigger and cures; transformed beings show their changed body.

**Context.** Actor lines carry afflictions known to the actor, with visibility.

### 52.95 Twenty-eight emotions

**Builds on.** `Emotion` (F6), `engine/mind/*`, needs, memories, acts, values.

**Current.** Twenty-four emotions. Surprise, curiosity, compassion and contempt are absent; acts of exploration, of mercy and of cruelty have no emotion to push them.

**Behaviour.** `surprise` follows unexpected happenings, is short and sharpens the next emotion; `curiosity` follows the unknown (new places, strangers, relics, anomalies) and pushes exploring, studying and contact; `compassion` follows others' suffering read through `mercy` and kinship values and pushes giving, healing and sparing; `contempt` follows those held lower or shamed, read through `hierarchy` and `purity` values, and pushes insult, exclusion and cruelty.

## Part 25. Batch 14 — hearts and hands

Batch 14 uses F70: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guard of F70 covers it.

### 52.106 Twenty-one relation types

**Builds on.** `RelationType` (F18 relations), kin roles (50.6), unions (50.8), spec 16 48.6 adoption and fosterage (`AdoptionKind`: heir, ward, foster, sponsor, blood bond, chosen kin), oaths, households, `engine/intrigue/schemes.py`.

**Current.** Eighteen types. Betrothal, sworn kinship and fosterage are absent, though a `propose` interaction exists and many cultures hold sworn kin and foster kin as close as blood.

**State.** `RelationType` gains `betrothed` (promised to a union), `sworn_kin` (bound as kin by oath or rite) and `foster` (one raised in the other's household, read both ways). The act that makes `sworn_kin` and `foster` is the spec 16 adoption record (`AdoptionKind.blood_bond`, `AdoptionKind.foster`); the relation type is the standing bond that record creates, so there is one record of the act and one of the bond (48.9). The relation catalogue gives each its opinion floor, duties, inheritance standing and how it ends.

**Behaviour.**

1. A `propose` accepted, or a match made by kin, sets `betrothed`; it becomes `spouse` at the union or ends by breaking, which brings grievance between houses and may be a matter for law.
2. `sworn_kin` comes from an adoption record of kind `blood_bond` made by an oath rite (blood, gifts, words by culture); it gives kin duties (vengeance, aid, hospitality) and, where culture says so, inheritance; breaking it is oathbreaking.
3. `foster` comes from an adoption record of kind `foster` under fosterage customs (hostage, alliance, apprenticeship, care of orphans); it binds two households and gives loyalty and claims.

**Rules.** Namespace `relations`: `betrothal_break_grievance` 30 [0–100], `sworn_kin_duty` 70 [0–100], `foster_loyalty` 50 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `relation.betrothed`, `relation.betrothal_broken`, `relation.sworn`, `relation.fostered`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `swear_kinship` (`target_id`, `rite`), `foster_child` (`child_id`, `household_id`); `propose` sets betrothal.

**God levers.** Relation editor offers twenty-one types.

**Screens.** Relations section with type medallions; family tree shows sworn and foster ties.

**Context.** Relation lines carry the type.

**Codex and book.** Entries list relations; house entries show sworn and foster ties.

**Reach.** Every being with relations, through `ThingSections`.

## Part 27. Batch 16 — many bodies

### 52.122 Sixteen biology variants

**Builds on.** `BiologyVariant` (F46), people biology, 52.47 diets, 52.49 biochemistries, 52.79 `colonial` plan, world types (`fungal`), `engine/cosmos/omens.py`.

**Current.** Twelve variants: incorporeal, aquatic, aerial, subterranean, hive, plant-like, construct, ageless, shapeshifting, gaseous, crystalline, undead. Fungal peoples, peoples whose bodies are colonies of members, peoples of energy and peoples that live joined to a host or partner species are absent. `SKYLESS` is hand-written.

**State.** `BiologyVariant` gains `fungal`, `colonial`, `energy` and `symbiotic`. The variant catalogue gives each its body plan, biochemistry, diet range, habitats, birth and death, population rate, war traits and how it meets other peoples; `SKYLESS` becomes its field.

**Behaviour.**

1. `fungal` peoples grow from spores, spread through soil and dead matter (decomposers, 52.57), thrive in dark and damp, and are harmed by dry heat and fire; their settlements can spread under the ground.
2. `colonial` peoples are bodies of many members (52.79): they lose members rather than lives, grow by budding, and decide as one within a body.
3. `energy` peoples feed on energy (52.47), are bound to sources (stars, fields, ley), are not touched by heat or cold (`athermic`, 52.61) and cannot hold matter without works.
4. `symbiotic` peoples live joined to a host or partner species: each body is a pair; the partner's health and range bind theirs, and the loss of the partner species is a catastrophe.
5. Every variant changes where a people can live, what it eats, how it fights, how it is born and dies, and how it shares land, markets and battlefields with others.

**Rules.** Namespace `biology`: `fungal_fire_harm_pct` 150 [0–500], `colonial_bud_rate` 5 [0–50], `energy_source_need` 30 [0–100], `symbiotic_partner_need` 50 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `people.partner_lost`, `people.budded`.

**Agent tools.** Son genesis and people tools list sixteen variants.

**God levers.** People biology editor offers sixteen.

**Screens.** Biology medallions in people drawers; the genesis wizard's people step.

**Context.** People lines carry the variant.

**Codex and book.** People entries show the variant and its consequences.

**Integrity.** A `symbiotic` people names its partner species; an `energy` people its sources.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every people.

**Couplings.** Diets, biochemistry, body plans, war, birth, trade, habitat.

## Part 28. Batch 17 — codes of honour

Batches 17–19 use F70: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guard of F70 covers it.

### 52.124 Fifty-eight judged acts

**Builds on.** `ActKind` (F8 ethics: each culture's stance on each act), `EthicStance`, values, sayings and doings (50.29), the acts made possible by spec 17.

**Current.** Fifty-two acts. Lying, drunkenness, robbing tombs, using charms, feeding on hosts and killing a sacred animal cannot be judged, though the engine now produces each of them (52.70, 52.90, 52.47, 51.21, the sacred animal trait).

**State.** `ActKind` gains `lying`, `drunkenness`, `tomb_robbing`, `using_charms`, `feeding_on_hosts` and `killing_sacred_animal`. Each culture holds a stance on each (forbidden to obligatory), derived from its values and authored by genesis or the model.

**Behaviour.**

1. Every engine path that performs one of these acts records it as an act of its doer, so ethics, standing, opinion and law read it: deceit in intrigue and trade is `lying`; intoxication past a threshold is `drunkenness`; robbing graves and hoards is `tomb_robbing`; brewing or casting a `charm` is `using_charms`; a `parasite` diet feeding is `feeding_on_hosts`; killing a species with the sacred trait is `killing_sacred_animal`.
2. The doer's own stance sets guilt and stress; witnesses' stances set opinion and reputation; the law sets punishment.
3. Sayings and doings (50.29) compare a person's professed values with these acts as with the others.

**Rules.** Namespace `ethics`: `drunkenness_threshold` 60 [0–100], `lying_detect_pct` 20 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `ethics.act_judged` with the act as a fact.

## Part 30. Batch 19 — the teeming millions

### 52.135 Cohorts by the biology's own sexes

**Builds on.** `demography/cohorts.py`, `vital.py`, `collective/demography.py`, biology sexes (F46), `MortalSex`, union axes (47.3.4), 50.8 reproductive course.

**Current.** Cohorts use a fixed `Sex` of two values (D22). Births count adult `female` cohorts; `widows` is `women − men`; the fertility transition reads `women_study`.

**State.** `Sex` goes. Cohorts are keyed by `sex_kind`: one of the sexes the people's biology defines (with `none` for biologies without sexes), each typed by its role in reproduction (`bears`, `begets`, `both`, `neither`). `sex_ratio` holds counts per sex kind. `widows` becomes `bereaved_partners`. `women_study` becomes `bearers_study` (education among those who bear young).

**Behaviour.**

1. Births count cohorts whose sex kind `bears` (or `both`); peoples that reproduce by budding, spores or making count every adult by their biology.
2. War losses fall on the cohorts the culture sends to war (its war roles by sex kind, class and age, authored and derived from values), not on any sex by default.
3. Bereaved partners are counted from unions ended by death, by sex kind.
4. The fertility transition reads education among bearers.

**Rules.** Namespace `demography`: unchanged keys; `war_role_default` none.

**Incidents.** None of their own.

**Agent tools.** Tools that read cohorts read sex kinds.

**God levers.** Cohort editor offers the biology's sex kinds; culture editor holds war roles.

**Screens.** Cohort pyramid by the biology's sexes; war roles table in culture drawers.

**Context.** Community lines carry cohorts by sex kind.

**Codex and book.** Settlement entries show the pyramid.

**Integrity.** Cohort sex kinds belong to the people's biology.

**Legacy.** The migration maps `female` and `male` cohorts to the biology's sex kinds where the biology has those two; other biologies' cohorts are re-split by their sexes.

**Reach.** Every settlement and people.

**Couplings.** Births, war losses, unions, education.

## Part 31. Batch 20 — many banners

Batches 20–22 use F70: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guard of F70 covers it.

### 52.142 Twelve identity layers

**Builds on.** `IdentityLayer` (belonging), `engine/belonging/*`, languages and speech communities, biology variants (52.122), made minds and mixed societies (44.19), movements (52.146).

**Current.** Nine layers: people, faith, class, locality, house, profession, generation, polity, circle. A speech community apart from a people, a kind of being (born, made, of another biology) and a cause held by movement members cannot be an identity.

**State.** `IdentityLayer` gains `language`, `kind` and `cause`. Each settlement, people and named mortal holds a value, a strength and a weight on each of the twelve.

**Behaviour.**

1. `language` identity forms around the tongue a community speaks (native, second, liturgical); it rises where a language is suppressed or revived and binds speakers across peoples and polities.
2. `kind` identity forms where beings of different kinds live together (born and made, peoples of different biologies); it rises with laws that treat kinds differently (44.6) and with contact.
3. `cause` identity forms in members of a movement (52.146) and holds them after the crowd that started it has gone.
4. Salience (52.143) can raise any of the twelve.

**Rules.** Namespace `identity`: per layer `{layer}_base_weight` (0–100); `identity.language_suppression_rise` 15 [0–100], `identity.kind_law_rise` 15 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `identity.rose` with the layer as a fact.

**Agent tools.** Mortal and son identity tools list twelve layers.

**God levers.** Identity editor offers twelve layers.

**Screens.** "Belonging" in `ThingSections`: the twelve layers as bars with value, strength and weight.

**Context.** Actor lines carry their salient layers.

**Codex and book.** Entries show identity layers.

**Integrity.** Values point to existing languages, kinds and movements.

**Legacy.** Fixup `identity.w52`: language layers from spoken languages; kind layers in mixed communities; cause layers for movement members.

**Reach.** Every settlement, people and named mortal or made mind.

**Couplings.** Languages, laws on kinds, movements.

Revivals hold a way and a goal.

**Behaviour.** `restore` revives language, gods and customs and clashes with rulers; `synthesis` founds a new faith or custom set around its prophet; `adopt` assimilates and ends the revival; `await` holds a people in readiness, with mass acts when a sign comes; `withdraw` founds separate settlements or quarters and lowers conflict until rulers press.

**Rules.** Namespace `revival`: per way `{way}_weight` (0–100).

## Part 34. Batch 23 — the gift

Batches 23–25 use F70: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guard of F70 covers it.

### 52.161 Thirteen gift occasions

**Builds on.** `GiftOccasion` (gift ledger, `engine/cycles/gifts.py`), naming rites (52.153), funerals, apology (52.107), patrons (52.164), hospitality.

**Current.** Eight occasions: courtesy, feast, circuit, offering, marriage, return, alliance, relief. Gifts at a birth, gifts of condolence at a funeral, gifts that make amends for a wrong, gifts of a patron to a client and the guest gift of hospitality are absent.

**State.** `GiftOccasion` gains `birth`, `funeral`, `amends`, `patronage` and `hospitality`. The occasion catalogue gives each its expected return, the debt it sets and the standing at stake.

**Behaviour.**

1. `birth` gifts come at naming rites from kin and patrons and bind the child to the givers.
2. `funeral` gifts come to the bereaved (not to the grave; grave goods are 51.21) and are owed back at the giver's own losses.
3. `amends` gifts settle a wrong (insult, harm, killing) by the culture's custom; accepted, they end grievance and feud; refused, they deepen it.
4. `patronage` gifts flow down from patrons to clients, artists and followers and are repaid in loyalty, service and praise, not in kind.
5. `hospitality` gifts pass between host and guest and seal guest right; breaking guest right after them is the gravest shame.

**Rules.** Namespace `gifts`: per occasion `{occasion}_debt` (0–100); `gifts.amends_grievance_cut` 60 [0–100], `gifts.patronage_loyalty` 10 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `gift.given` with the occasion as a fact.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `give_gift` (`target_id`, `item`, `occasion`) lists thirteen.

**God levers.** Gift ledger editor offers thirteen occasions.

**Screens.** "Gifts" in `ThingSections`: the ledger with occasion medallions, open debts first.

**Context.** Actor lines carry open gift debts.

**Codex and book.** Entries list notable gifts and debts.

**Integrity.** A gift names giver, receiver and item.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every being, house, people and god that gives or receives, through `ThingSections`.

**Couplings.** Naming, funerals, feuds, patrons, guest right.

### 52.162 Eight gift states

**Builds on.** `GiftState` (open, returned, refused, destroyed, lapsed), gift circuits.

**Current.** Five states. A gift returned with more than was given, a gift passed on along a circuit and a gift whose debt the giver releases are absent, though rivalry by outgiving and circuits that pass gifts on are both described.

**State.** `GiftState` gains `exceeded`, `passed_on` and `released`.

**Behaviour.** `exceeded` returns more than was given, puts the first giver in debt and can start a rivalry of outgiving that drains both houses and raises their standing; `passed_on` moves a circuit gift to the next people in the circuit's order and keeps the circuit's peace; `released` ends a debt by the giver's grace, raising the giver's standing and the receiver's loyalty.

**Rules.** Namespace `gifts`: `exceed_ratio_pct` 150 [100–500], `rivalry_drain_pct` 10 [0–100], `release_loyalty` 15 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `gift.exceeded`, `gift.passed_on`, `gift.released`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `return_gift` (`gift_id`, `amount`) and `release_debt` (`gift_id`).

**God levers.** Gift ledger editor offers eight states.

**Screens.** State badges in the gift ledger.

**Context.** Actor lines carry gift states.

**Codex and book.** Entries record gift rivalries and circuits.

**Integrity.** A `passed_on` gift belongs to a circuit.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every gift.

**Couplings.** Rivalry, standing, circuits, loyalty.

Batches 26–27 use F70: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guard of F70 covers `NumeralBase`, `LanguageModality`, `LanguageStage`, `SenseShift`, `WordRegister`, `ScriptChangeCause`, `WritingMedium`, `LanguagePolicy`, `SociolectKind`, `SignCause`, `AccountKind` and `AccountStance`.

### 52.173 Six numeral bases

**Builds on.** Languages (`engine/tongues/*`), numeracy (`crafts/reckoning.py`), calendars, measures and trade.

**Current.** A language has grammatical number but no counting base; how a people counts does not bear on its numeracy, calendars or measures.

**State.** `NumeralBase`: `decimal`, `vigesimal`, `duodecimal`, `sexagesimal`, `octal`, `body_tally` (counting along parts of the body). `languages.numeral_base`. The base catalogue gives each its divisibility and reckoning ease.

**Behaviour.** Numeracy reads the base: bases with many divisors (12, 60) ease fractions in trade, astronomy and calendars (month and hour divisions); `body_tally` limits large reckoning until a written system grows. Number words in generated names and texts follow the base. Contact can carry a base between languages.

**Rules.** Namespace `tongues`: per base `{base}_reckoning_pct` (0–200).

**Builds on.** `LanguageModality` (vocal, sign, scent, colour, telepathic, data, chemical), senses (52.59), biology variants.

**Current.** Seven modalities. Languages of touch, of vibration through ground or water and of electric fields cannot be spoken.

**State.** `LanguageModality` gains `tactile`, `vibration` and `electric`.

**Behaviour.** `tactile` languages need contact and work in darkness and among those without sight or hearing; `vibration` languages carry through ground or water and suit subterranean and aquatic peoples, and can be overheard by those with the vibration sense; `electric` languages work at short range in water and need the electric sense (52.59). Intelligibility between modalities needs interpreters or works.

**Rules.** Namespace `tongues`: `vibration_range` 3 [0–20], `electric_range` 1 [0–10].

## Part 40. Batch 29 — coin of the realm

Batches 29–31 use F70 and F71: every enum below has a `total()` catalogue, and the guards cover it.

### 52.200 Six credit states

**Builds on.** `CreditState` (normal, strained, default, restructuring) of polities, monetary authorities (51.5), leagues (51.7), revolutions.

**Current.** Four states. A polity rescued by another power and a polity that repudiates its debts are absent.

**State.** `CreditState` gains `rescued` (debts carried by another polity, league or lender on terms) and `repudiated` (debts declared void).

**Behaviour.** `rescued` polities keep paying under the rescuer's terms, lose sovereignty over budgets and owe the rescuer standing; `repudiated` debts stop at once, lenders lose them, the polity is shut out of credit for `credit.repudiation_epochs` and its creditors' polities may take it as a casus belli.

**Rules.** Namespace `credit`: `repudiation_years` 30 [0–500], `rescue_sovereignty_cut` 20 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `credit.rescued`, `credit.repudiated`.

**Agent tools.** Ruler `repudiate_debts`; `rescue_polity` (`polity_id`, `terms`).

**God levers.** Credit editor offers six states.

**Screens.** Treasury panel credit badge.

**Context.** Polity lines carry credit state.

**Codex and book.** Polity entries record credit history.

**Integrity.** `rescued` names its rescuer.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every polity with debts.

**Couplings.** Leagues, war, sovereignty, lenders.

### 52.201 Seven loan states

**Builds on.** `LoanStatus` (open, repaid, defaulted, forgiven), collateral, inheritance.

**Current.** Four states. Loans whose terms are changed, loans whose collateral is taken and loans sold to another lender are absent.

**State.** `LoanStatus` gains `rescheduled`, `collateral_seized` and `sold`. Loans hold `collateral` (holding, goods or person under the law of bound labour).

**Behaviour.** `rescheduled` changes rate and term by agreement; `collateral_seized` moves the collateral to the lender on default where law allows; `sold` moves the loan to a new lender at a discount, who collects it.

**Rules.** Namespace `credit`: `sale_discount_pct` 30 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `loan.rescheduled`, `loan.collateral_seized`, `loan.sold`.

**Agent tools.** Mortal `reschedule_loan`, `sell_loan`.

**God levers.** Loan editor offers seven states.

**Screens.** Loan list in holder drawers.

**Context.** Holder lines carry loans.

**Codex and book.** Holder entries.

**Integrity.** `collateral_seized` names its collateral.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every loan.

**Couplings.** Law, bound labour, debt trade.

### 52.208 Seven trade route media in one taxonomy

**Builds on.** `TradeMode` (road, river, sea, caravan, sky), `RouteEnvironment` (sea, land, air, space, rift, network), `CarrierKind` (47.2.4), spec 16 48.9.

**Current.** Two enums name a route's medium (D28); `caravan` is a carrier.

**State.** `TradeMode` becomes the one taxonomy: `road`, `river`, `sea`, `sky`, `space`, `rift`, `network`. `RouteEnvironment` goes; its readers read `TradeMode` (`land` → `road`, `air` → `sky`). Routes that were `caravan` become `road` routes served by pack carriers (`CarrierKind.pack_animals` or `porters`).

**Behaviour.** A route's medium sets which carriers can use it, its hazards and its speed; carriers (47.2.4) carry the goods.

### 52.238 Six kinds of criminal organisation

**Builds on.** The criminal kinds of `FactionKind` and `FoundableFaction` (crime family, thieves' guild, smuggling ring, pirate confederacy), rackets, youth groups (50.11), trafficking.

**Current.** Four kinds. Street gangs of the young and rings that traffic people are absent as organisations, though youth groups of crime and the trafficking racket exist.

**State.** Built-in organisation kinds (spec 16 48.6) of purpose `crime` gain `street_gang` and `trafficking_ring` (D37), each with ranks, treasury and the rackets it runs.

**Behaviour.** `street_gang` recruits from youth groups of crime and from slums and camps, fights for single streets, and grows into a family or is absorbed by one; `trafficking_ring` runs the trafficking racket along routes and borders, feeding bound labour and kidnapping, and draws the harshest suppression where law and values forbid it.

### 52.239 Four state stances toward crime

**Builds on.** `CrimeStance` (suppress, co-opt), bribery, licences (letters of marque).

**Current.** Two stances. Looking away for bribes and licensing a trade outright are absent.

**State.** `CrimeStance` gains `tolerate` and `license`.

**Behaviour.** `tolerate` lets organisations work for bribes and order kept quiet; corruption rises and so does the risk of an outcry; `license` makes a trade lawful under terms (privateers, gaming houses, intoxicant sellers), taxing it and binding its holders to the polity.

**Builds on.** `FugitiveKind` (outlaw, accused, defector), bound labour, armies, faiths.

**Current.** Three kinds. Runaways from bound labour, deserters and those hunted for their faith are absent.

**State.** `FugitiveKind` gains `runaway`, `deserter` and `heretic`.

**Behaviour.** `runaway` fugitives flee bondage and are hunted by owners and law; `deserter` fugitives leave armies and are hunted by them; `heretic` fugitives flee a faith's persecution. Each seeks the sanctuaries that take them (52.241).

### 52.241 Six kinds of sanctuary

**Builds on.** `SanctuaryKind` (temple, hospitality, asylum), wild terrain, city charters, embassies.

**Current.** Three kinds. Refuge in the wilds, the freedom a chartered city gives after a stay and refuge in an embassy are absent.

**State.** `SanctuaryKind` gains `wilds`, `free_city` and `embassy`.

Disruptions include: long winters and summers by every cause (52.3), late frost and ice storms (52.2), mudslides, flash floods and thin ice (52.19), river shifts (52.32), upwelling failure (52.39), swarm strikes and feral herds (52.48, 52.50), keystone losses (52.58), gangrene in a ruler (52.82), charms and fortune curses (52.90), grief turning to vengeance (52.96), exodus and boycotts (52.149), beast waking by theft (52.69), routes closing by season (52.209), mutinies over pay (52.303), impacts by wreck and airburst (52.384, 52.385). Recoveries include: fairs and wild harvests (52.5), fish ponds (52.44), sanitation (52.76), relief and pensions (52.222), mediation of crises and treaties (52.271, 52.273), released gift debts (52.162), amends ending feuds (52.161), honest paymasters (52.303). ## Part 100. Deepening pass — batches 1–10

Batches 1–10 were written once as a check of counts. This pass reads every value of them again for depth, including those first called complete, and widens each where the world gains a mechanic from it. Every enum here has a `total()` catalogue under F70, and every widened column has its enum check rebuilt.

### 52.426 Five water readings of a season and the onset of every season

**Builds on.** 52.1 `season_phase` (`SeasonWarmth` 7, `SeasonWater` `dry`, `even`, `wet`), calendar slots (52.5), sowing.

**Current.** A season is dry, even or wet, and every season arrives on time every year.

**State.** `SeasonWater` becomes `arid`, `dry`, `even`, `wet`, `deluge`. `SeasonOnset` (`early`, `on_time`, `late`, `failed`) is drawn each year per world and season into `season_onsets` (world, year, season, onset, by_node_id, locked); a `failed` season does not bring its water.

**Behaviour.** Onset shifts the calendar slots that open in that season (sowing, harvest, wild harvest, market), harvests, grazing, river levels and hunger. A failed wet season reads as a drought year for named years (52.4) and long seasons (52.3). Peoples with weather lore or almanacs forecast the onset.

**Rules.** Namespace `seasons`: `early_pct` 10, `late_pct` 10, `failed_pct` 3 [0–100]; `onset_yield_shift_pct` 15 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `season.onset` with the season and onset as facts.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the season tools read them.

**God levers.** The season editor offers every new value, and its rule keys are editable in the rules panel; held rows stay as set.

**Screens.** The season card and drawer section show and edit every new value with its label and icon.

**Context.** The season lines name the new values.

**Codex and book.** The season entries carry the new values with labels.

**Integrity.** Every value in its enum and its catalogue row.

**Legacy.** Fixup `seasons.w52b`: every past year reads `on_time`.

**Reach.** Every world where the season system runs.

**Couplings.** Calendar, harvest, rivers, hunger, named years.

### 52.427 Twenty-five weather kinds and eleven weather effects

**Builds on.** 52.2 (`frost`, `ice_storm`), F60 weather traits and draws, battle tables.

**Current.** No drizzle, sleet, freezing fog, thunderstorm, tornado or great circling storm; no effect for lightning, flood water or breathable air.

**State.** `WeatherKind` gains `drizzle`, `sleet`, `freezing_fog`, `thunderstorm`, `tornado`, `cyclone`, each with its F60 draw and traits. `WeatherEffect` gains `lightning` (strike harm and fires), `flood` (water rise on low ground and rivers) and `breath` (air fit to breathe: smoke, dust, gas). Every weather kind gives a weight for all eleven effects.

**Behaviour.** `thunderstorm` sets fires on dry ground and strikes high places; `tornado` strikes one region along a track and breaks structures; `cyclone` is a named storm that crosses sea and coast for several turns, raising storm surge (52.437) and floods; `freezing_fog` ices rigging and roads; `sleet` and `drizzle` wet without heavy flooding. `breath` lowers work, travel and health for bodies by their breath system (50.25).

**Rules.** Namespace `weather`: per kind `{kind}_weight` (0–100); `cyclone_turns` 3 [1–10]; `lightning_fire_pct` 8 [0–100].

**Incidents.** `weather.cyclone` (named, with track), `weather.tornado`, `weather.lightning`.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the weather tools read them.

**God levers.** The weather editor offers every new value, and its rule keys are editable in the rules panel; held rows stay as set.

**Screens.** The weather card and drawer section show and edit every new value with its label and icon.

**Context.** The weather lines name the new values.

**Codex and book.** The weather entries carry the new values with labels.

**Integrity.** Every value in its enum and its catalogue row.

**Legacy.** Constraint rebuild on every column typed by `WeatherKind` and `WeatherEffect`.

**Reach.** Every world where the weather system runs.

**Couplings.** Fire, coasts, structures, battle, body systems.

**Rules.** Namespace `soils`: `permafrost_thaw_pct` 5 [0–100].

### 52.456 Ten catch grounds and twelve kinds of gear

**Builds on.** 52.44, 52.45.

**Current.** No paused development and no warm core with cold limbs.

**State.** `Dormancy` gains `diapause`. `Thermoregulation` gains `mesotherm`.

**Behaviour.** `diapause` pauses growth of young or eggs until a season returns, so a species survives a failed season (52.426) and returns in numbers; `mesotherm` bodies keep a warm core with cooler limbs, active in cold water and air at less food than endotherms.

**Rules.** Namespace `dormancy`: `diapause_survival_pct` 60 [0–100]; `mesotherm_food_pct` 70 [0–100].

### 52.482 Thirteen spread paths and fifteen plague responses

**Builds on.** 52.75, 52.76.

**Current.** No spread with moved herds or a shared water supply; no fleeing, inoculating or closing gatherings.

**State.** `SpreadPath` gains `livestock` and `water_supply`. `PlagueResponse` gains `flee`, `inoculate` and `close_gatherings`.

**Behaviour.** `livestock` spreads disease where herds are moved, sold and driven; `water_supply` spreads it through shared wells, aqueducts and cisterns, so one source sickens a city. `flee` sends the able out of a sick city (spreading the disease and emptying the city), `inoculate` lowers the toll where the tier allows, and `close_gatherings` stops feasts, markets and rites at a cost in morale and trade.

**Rules.** Namespace `plague`: per response `{response}_effect` (0–100).

**Incidents.** `plague.response` with the response.

## Part 101. Deepening pass — batches 11–20

Every value of batches 11–20 is read again for depth, including those first called complete. Every enum here has a `total()` catalogue under F70 and every widened column has its enum check rebuilt. Values with no change are named at the end with their reason.

### 52.491 Twenty effect package categories

**Builds on.** 52.90 (`fortune`, `transformation`, `charm` on fourteen), F30.

**Current.** No package changes how fast a being ages, takes its memories or holds it in a sleep it cannot leave.

**State.** `PackageKind` gains `ageing` (ageing sped, slowed or stopped, with `ageing_rate_pct`), `forgetting` (memories, skills or a person's name taken, with `forget_scope`: `recent`, `person`, `skill`, `all`) and `sleep` (a sleep that holds until its cure, with `sleep_until`: a time, a deed, a person's act).

**Behaviour.** `ageing` moves the holder through life stages at its rate and changes death by old age; `forgetting` removes the holder's memories (MemoryKind rows), relations' opinion history or skill levels in its scope, and they can be relearned; `sleep` removes the holder from every act while the body needs care, and heirs, offices and unions read the sleeper as absent. Sacred-site vengeance and curses can install all twenty.

**Rules.** Namespace `packages`: `ageing_rate_pct` 200 [0–1000], `forget_share_pct` 50 [0–100], `sleep_care_cost` 3 [0–50].

**Incidents.** `affliction.aged`, `affliction.forgot`, `affliction.slept`, `affliction.woke`.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the affliction tools read them.

**God levers.** The affliction editor offers every new value, and its rule keys are editable in the rules panel; held rows stay as set.

**Context.** The affliction lines name the new values.

**Codex and book.** The affliction entries carry the new values with labels.

**Integrity.** Every value in its enum and its catalogue row.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every world where the affliction system runs.

**Couplings.** Life stages, memory, offices, succession.

## Part 102. Deepening pass — batches 21–30, and corrections

### 52.530 Corrections to earlier batches (D30–D35)

Reading batches 21–30 against spec 16 found values that spec 17 adds twice or names with images. Each is corrected here and closed by a guard.

| Defect | What was wrong | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| D30 | Spec 17 named new values with words of the imagery families that spec 16 48.8 renamed out of `SoilKind` (`salt`, `bone`): `TerrainKind.salt_flat`, `RockKind.rock_salt`, `SedimentKind.salt`, `CommodityKind.salt`, `WorkshopKind.saltworks`, `ProcessKind.salt_making`, `WritingMedium.bone`, `MaterialKind` and beast product `great_beast_bone`. **Guard.** `scripts/check_spec_duplicates.py` (on every commit that touches `docs/spec`): it reads every "`Enum` gains …" and every value list of every spec and fails when a later spec adds a value an earlier spec already holds for the same enum, or counts an enum differently from the latest spec that widens it. `scripts/spec_coverage.py` runs it.

### 52.531 Fifteen crowd acts, seven crowd feelings and nineteen triggers

**Builds on.** 52.149–52.151.

**Current.** No silent vigil, occupation of a place or petition; crowds feel no joy or solidarity; rising prices, the arrest of a loved figure and omens do not start crowds.

**State.** `CollectiveActKind` gains `vigil`, `occupation` and `petition`. `CrowdFeeling` gains `joy` and `solidarity` (rows of `crowd_feelings`). `CollectiveTrigger` gains `price_rise`, `arrest` and `omen`.

**Behaviour.** `vigil` gathers in grief or hope without harm and raises the feeling it carries; `occupation` holds a square, a workplace or a building until met or cleared, stopping its work; `petition` carries a demand to a ruler or council, who answer, refuse or punish, and the answer moves legitimacy. `joy` feeds jubilation and gatherings; `solidarity` lowers the threshold of strikes and boycotts and raises mutual aid (52.509). `price_rise` reads market prices (52.42), `arrest` the jailing of a figure with high renown, `omen` sky events and omens (52.4).

**Rules.** Namespace `crowds`: per act `{act}_threshold` (0–100); per feeling `{feeling}_decay` (0–100); per trigger `{trigger}_push` (0–100).

**Incidents.** `crowd.acted` with the act; `petition.answered` with the answer.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the crowd tools read them.

**God levers.** The crowd editor offers every new value, and its rule keys are editable in the rules panel; held rows stay as set.

**Screens.** The crowd card and drawer section show and edit every new value with its label and icon.

**Context.** The crowd lines name the new values.

**Codex and book.** The crowd entries carry the new values with labels.

**Integrity.** Every value in its enum and its catalogue row.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every world where the crowd system runs.

**Couplings.** Prices, renown, omens, legitimacy.

### 52.532 Twenty-three tradition functions, eight rite-of-passage stages and sixteen tradition effects

**Builds on.** Spec 16 48.7 (`TraditionFunction` 19 with `purification`, `commemoration`, `competition`; rite of passage stages `birth`, `naming`, `coming_of_age`, `union`, `elderhood`, `death`), 52.153 (corrected by D31 to add `fair`), 52.5 effects.

**Current.** No rite of welcome for strangers, of reconciliation or of thanksgiving; no rite for entering an order or for leaving home; traditions do not heal or bind those who keep them.

**State.** `TraditionFunction` gains `welcome`, `reconciliation` and `thanksgiving`. Rite of passage stages gain `initiation` (into an order, guild or society) and `departure` (leaving home or one's people). `TraditionEffectKind` gains `healing` (health of participants) and `bonding` (relations among participants).

**Behaviour.** `welcome` rites turn strangers into guests (52.508 `guest_friend`) and lower suspicion of newcomers; `reconciliation` rites end feuds and grudges when both sides keep them (52.161 `amends`); `thanksgiving` follows plenty, peace and recovery and raises piety and cohesion. `initiation` gives standing in the order; `departure` gives the leaver gifts and kin ties that hold across distance.

**Rules.** Per function its cost and slot fit; per effect its weight.

**Incidents.** `tradition.kept` as built.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the tradition tools read them.

### 52.538 Eight numeral bases, twelve modalities and seven language stages

**Builds on.** 52.173–52.175.

**Current.** No base five or base two; no whistled or drummed speech carried far; no stage for a language with few speakers left.

**State.** `NumeralBase` gains `quinary` and `binary`. `LanguageModality` gains `whistled` and `drummed` (carried over distance). `LanguageStage` gains `endangered`.

**Behaviour.** `quinary` counting is easy to learn and slow for large sums; `binary` counting serves made minds, networks and reckoning machines. `whistled` and `drummed` speech carry messages across valleys, forests and seas faster than runners, as an alternative to relays in worlds without networks, and are read by those who know the language. An `endangered` language has few speakers left: its speakers' identity rises, revival policies (52.180) and movements gain draw, and its death on the last speaker's death becomes a `language.died` incident.

**Rules.** Namespace `tongues`: `whistle_range` 3 [1–20] regions; `endangered_speakers` 500 [1–100000].

**Incidents.** `language.endangered`.

### 52.539 Nine sense shifts, nine registers, seven script causes, sixteen media, seven policies, ten sociolects and six sign causes

**Behaviour.** `reversed` shifts turn a word's meaning to its opposite over generations and can break old treaties and laws read in new ways; `slang` marks youth and outsiders and changes fast; `legal` registers raise success in courts for those who command them. `technology` changes scripts with printing and machines (52.542). `cloth` records are light and burn; `potsherd` records are cheap and last. `bilingual` policy keeps two languages official and raises both. `clergy` and `scholars` sociolects mark their speakers and keep old words. `noise` sign languages arise among workers in loud workplaces.

**Rules.** Per value `{value}_weight` (0–100).

### 52.544 Seven credit states, eight loan states, six forms of saving, eight covers, five speculation states, four plays and eleven trade policies

**Builds on.** 52.200–52.205, 47.3.5.

**Current.** No credit cut off by sanctions; no loan passed to heirs; no herd held as savings; no health or ransom cover; no hoard that spoils; no selling short; no tolls or staple rights.

**State.** `CreditState` gains `frozen`. `LoanStatus` gains `inherited`. `SavingForm` gains `livestock`. `InsuranceCover` gains `health` and `ransom`. `SpeculationStatus` gains `spoiled`. `MarketPlay` gains `short`. `TradePolicyKind` gains `toll` and `staple_right` (goods must be offered first in a town's market).

**Behaviour.** `frozen` credit follows sanctions: the polity cannot borrow abroad until lifted. `inherited` loans pass to heirs by the inheritance custom and can bind them under bound labour law. `livestock` savings grow by breeding and fall by disease and theft. `health` cover pays for treatment; `ransom` cover pays for captives. `spoiled` hoards lose their goods by spoilage. `short` plays sell borrowed goods and gain when prices fall. `toll` policies charge passage on routes and bridges; `staple_right` makes passing goods be offered first in a town's market.

**Rules.** Per value `{value}_rate` (0–100).

**Incidents.** None of their own.

### 52.549 Eleven reasons for labour allocation and thirteen shortfalls

**Builds on.** 52.215, 52.216.

**Current.** Work is not set by debt or by duty to kin; lack of schooling and of justice are no shortfalls.

**State.** `LabourReason` gains `debt` (a debtor works the creditor's work, 52.544 `inherited`) and `kin_duty` (household and kin assign work by role). `ShortfallEffect` gains `learning` (no school or teacher in reach) and `justice` (no court in reach, wrongs unanswered).

**Behaviour.** Debt labour lowers the debtor's freedom and raises grievance and flight; kin duty follows the culture's household roles with no default by sex. A learning shortfall lowers skills of the young and raises the youth `learning` purpose; a justice shortfall raises feuds and self-help violence and the need `justice` (52.498).

**Rules.** Namespace `labour`: `debt_share_pct` 30 [0–100]; per shortfall `{shortfall}_weight` (0–100).

**Incidents.** `shortfall.felt` as built.

**Agent tools.** Son and mortal tools that list these enums list the new values; the labour tools read them.

**God levers.** The labour editor offers every new value, and its rule keys are editable in the rules panel; held rows stay as set.

**Context.** The labour lines name the new values.

**Codex and book.** The labour entries carry the new values with labels.

**Integrity.** Every value in its enum and its catalogue row.

**Legacy.** None.

**Reach.** Every world where the labour system runs.

### 52.550 Twenty-seven district kinds, eleven zones, thirteen housing levels and twenty-three services

**Builds on.** 52.219, zones, housing, services.

**Current.** No quarter for pilgrims or caravans, and none built on water; no port zone; no level below the hut or a palace on the ladder; no street lighting or pest control.

**State.** `DistrictKind` gains `pilgrim_quarter`, `caravan_quarter` and `floating`. `ZoneKind` gains `port`. `HousingLevel` gains `shack` (below `hut`) and `palace` (above `manor`). `UrbanService` gains `lighting` and `pest_control`.

**Behaviour.** Pilgrim quarters house pilgrims at the `pilgrimage` slot and spread news and disease; caravan quarters house traders at a city's edge and raise trade and foreign contact; floating districts rest on rafts or boats on lakes and rivers and rise with floods. Port zones hold docks and customs. Shacks house the displaced in camps; palaces house rulers and courts. Lighting lowers crime at night and raises the night economy; pest control lowers vermin, plague and crop loss in stores.

**Rules.** Per value its cost and effect.

**Incidents.** None of their own.

### 52.564 Six party roles, eight treaty states, six crisis states, six standings and nine council resolutions

**Builds on.** 52.271–52.275.

**Current.** No god or power stands witness to a pact; a treaty cannot be under renegotiation; a crisis cannot freeze; no polity stands apart from all; councils do not keep peace or recognise new polities.

**State.** `PartyRole` gains `witness` (a god, a power or an institution that sees the pact kept). `TreatyStatus` gains `renegotiating`. `CrisisState` gains `frozen` (neither side moves; costs run on). `RegionalStanding` gains `isolated`. `ResolutionKind` gains `peacekeeping` and `recognition`.

**Behaviour.** A witness punishes breach by its own means (a god's displeasure, a court's ruling) and raises the cost of breaking; renegotiation holds a treaty in force while terms move; frozen crises raise upkeep and unrest on both sides until one moves; isolated polities trade little and are seldom joined in wars; peacekeeping sends a force between parties; recognition admits a new polity to councils and treaties.

**Rules.** Namespace `diplomacy`: `witness_breach_cost` 20 [0–100]; `frozen_upkeep` 3 [0–20].

**Incidents.** `treaty.renegotiated`, `polity.recognised`.

### 52.592 Thirteen spell techniques, twenty-three forms and nine rite components

**Builds on.** Spell techniques, forms (spec 16 45.3 widened to 21), components.

**Current.** No technique heals, moves a thing or a being from place to place, or speaks across distance; no form works on dreams or on the world's own laws and oaths; no component is something given up, and none needs several workers together.

**State.** `SpellTechnique` gains `heal`, `move` and `speak`. `SpellForm` gains `dream` and `law` (the laws, oaths and pacts of a world and its peoples). `RiteComponent` gains `offered` (something given up: goods, time, strength, years) and `communal` (needs several workers at once).

**Behaviour.** `heal` restores injuries and conditions by form (body, mind, spirit) at the rite's cost and is judged by each culture's ethics where it competes with healers; `move` shifts beings and goods between places by range (52.349) and is blocked by wards; `speak` sends words by range and competes with messengers and networks. `dream` workings enter dreams (52.420 `dream`, 52.501) and shape them; `law` workings bind or loosen oaths, pacts and seals and are checked by witnesses (52.564). `offered` components draw cost from the offering in place of the caster; `communal` components raise power by the number of workers and spread the strain.

**Rules.** Namespace `arcana`: per technique `{technique}_cost` (0–100); `communal_power_per_worker` 10 [0–50].

**Incidents.** `rite.worked` with technique and form.

### 52.634 Twelve power origins, seventeen sources, eight states and nine triggers

**Builds on.** Spec 16 W45 innate powers.

**Current.** No power comes from an outer bargain or is taken from another being; no power draws on a people's memory or on names; no power is bound by another's seal; no power wakes in sleep or when others are in danger.

**State.** `PowerOrigin` gains `bargain` (52.607) and `transfer` (taken from another being by death, rite or device). `SourceLocus` gains `memory` (what a people remembers) and `name` (names and true names). `PowerState` gains `bound` (held by a seal, a geas or a device of another). `PowerTrigger` gains `sleep` and `others_in_danger`.

**Behaviour.** Bargain powers carry the outer being's terms and hazards; transferred powers leave the first holder without them and can be fought over; memory-sourced powers grow with remembrance and fade with forgetting (52.585); name-sourced powers work on those whose names are known (52.593 `only_by_name`); bound powers return when the binding breaks; sleep triggers act in dreams (52.501); others-in-danger triggers wake for kin, friends or charges.

**Rules.** Namespace `powers`: `transfer_loss_pct` 30 [0–100]; `memory_source_rate` 5 [0–50].

**Incidents.** `power.transferred`, `power.bound`.

**Behaviour.** Hybridising mixes the traits of two lines in their young and can give vigour or sterility; wild release lets the wild select a line over generations, fast and beyond the makers' control; light-making lines light settlements and works; inherited learning lines pass skills to their young; filtering lines clean water and air and lower pollution; building lines grow walls, shells and roads (52.523 `grown` dwellings); crosses-wild lines spread their traits into wild kin, for good or harm; exceeded lines carry gifts beyond their design and can escape their makers' control.

## Part 111. Integration plan for W52

Spec 17 is integrated as wave W52 in nine sub-waves. Each sub-wave is built whole, then audited across every layer of spec 16 6.6, then gated once; no sub-wave starts while another sub-wave's gate runs. The sections each sub-wave holds are named by number, so every section of this spec has exactly one home.

### 52.660 Order of work

| Sub-wave | Holds | Sections |
|---|---|---|
| W52.0 Groundwork | coverage and guards; every defect fix that the later sub-waves build on | 0.2 (coverage), F59–F71, D1–D40, 52.530 and 52.548 (correction guards), `check_spec_duplicates.py`, 17.B |
| W52.1 Land, sky and weather | seasons, weather, calendar, land, stone, winds, cycles, space weather, tolerances, weather works, observation, local climates | 52.1–52.41, 52.426–52.451, 52.653–52.657, F72, 52.663–52.668 |
| W52.2 Living things | farming and catch, species, plants, beasts, disease, the body | 52.42–52.89, 52.452–52.490 |
| W52.3 Minds and lives | packages, the inner life, the life course, relations, daily life, biology, honour, kinship, cohorts, identity | 52.90–52.148, 52.491–52.529 |
| W52.4 Culture and trade | crowds, traditions, gifts, art, clubs, tongues, accounts, materials, industry, finance, routes, goods, money, cuisine, dress, households, media, speech, works, commerce | 52.149–52.214, 52.531–52.547, 52.642–52.646, 52.649–52.652 |
| W52.5 Society and state | labour, cities, works, relics, crime, statecraft, membership, titles, law, factions | 52.215–52.270, 52.549–52.563 |
| W52.6 Diplomacy, intrigue and war | treaties, rise and ruin, messages, knowledge and belief, intrigue, espionage, armies, battles, sieges, war, vehicles, duels, feuds | 52.271–52.327, 52.564–52.582 |
| W52.7 Faith, magic and the gods | faith, prophecy, the afterlife, spirits, luck, divination, the arcanum, myth, made beings, worship, dominion, the council, apotheosis, natural law, the Creator, the outer dark | 52.328–52.379, 52.583–52.607 |
| W52.8 Cosmos, minds and the hidden | worlds, impacts, ends, travel, phenomena, prehistory, knowledge and eras, the storyteller, expeditions, the boundless, made minds, augments, networks, abundance, powers, hidden truths, living craft, incident steps | 52.380–52.425, 52.608–52.641, 52.647–52.648, 52.658–52.659 |

Within a sub-wave the steps are: coverage rows; guards (listing every current violation); enum values and the migration that rebuilds the enum checks of every typed column; `total()` catalogue rows; engine readers in the named phases; rule keys with defaults, ranges and bands; tool texts and context; API views and `npm run typegen`; label maps, editors and screens; the Codex and the book; fixups; proving tests; the audit; one gate.

### 52.661 Guards of W52

- `scripts/spec_coverage.py`, `scripts/check_spec_depth.py` and `scripts/check_inventory.py` read this file; `17-coverage.md` is written and gated (0.2). The depth check counts sections whose titles name an audit as complete by their nature, as it does for spec 16.
- `scripts/check_spec_duplicates.py`: no value is added twice, by this spec or over specs 13 and 16, in "gains" sentences or in value lists; no new value carries a word of the bias families of `check_prompt_bias.py` (D30, D38, D39, D40).
- One literal-set guard, `scripts/check_literal_enum_sets.py`, holds the family table of F59–F71: weather, terrain, movement, deep, catch, species, body, life (F70), goods (F71). It fails on any literal collection or mapping of two or more members of a family's enums outside the family's catalogue, migrations and tests. The per-family guards named in F59–F71 (`check_weather_sets.py`, `check_terrain_sets.py`, `check_deep_sets.py`, `check_catch_sets.py`, `check_species_sets.py`, `check_body_sets.py`, `check_life_sets.py`, `check_goods_sets.py`) are its families, not separate scripts, so the gate reads the source once. `check_season_positions.py`, `check_calendar_slots.py`, `check_movement_modes.py` and `check_cycle_fields.py` check more than sets and stay their own.
- The existing gates carry the rest: `check_enum_values_read.py` and `check_enum_constraints.py` (every new value read; every typed column's check rebuilt), `test_tool_enum_lists.py` and `test_catalogue.py` (tool texts list and describe every value), `check_label_maps.py` and `check_raw_enums.mjs` (every value labelled), `test_editable_fields.py` and `test_every_lever.py` (every value offered and editable), `test_frontend_types.py` (typegen), `check_wiring.py` and `check_control.py` (Codex, book and god control), `check_prompt_bias.py` with its enum scan (47.6.8), `test_god_control.py` and `test_eager_epochs.py` (held nodes and rare branches).

### 52.662 Acceptance of W52

Every rule key of the spec is in its namespace with default, range and band. W52 is done when every row of `17-coverage.md` is `done`, every value of Appendix 17.A is read by the engine, offered by a god lever and a screen, listed by its tools, labelled in the frontend, the Codex and the book, and reached by its proving test, every defect D1–D42 is closed with its test and guard, and the last sub-wave's audit finds nothing.
